jobs.description:
Doctoral Researcher in Food Processing for Planetary and Human Health

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Sustainable Food Processing Group focuses on advancing food processing technologies and their role in sustainable food systems, using innovative approaches to tackle fundamental challenges such as the protein transition and food security. We use innovative sustainability assessment and emerging food system approaches as key tools to guide processing innovations toward holistic and impactful solutions.

Job description

We are looking for a:

• Highly motivated candidate to join a collaborative research project that explores how food processing affects both nutritional quality and environmental impact.

The overall vision is to identify and develop processing strategies that improve nutritional quality and environmental performance as assessed by nutritional life cycle assessment (nLCA) while creating appealing hybrid protein-rich products. Thus, in addition to executing processing trials, the role includes coordinating collaborations within the team and with external partners to ensure that nutritional, health, and sustainability aspects are systematically integrated into the research.

Our two well-equipped pilot plants, featuring technologies ranging from multi-scale extruders to high-pressure and thermal treatment systems, pulsed electric field (PEF) equipment, and more, will serve as the core experimental platform for the project. Advanced analytical methods (e.g., nutritional profile, bioaccessibility, dynamic mechanical analysis, imaging, spectroscopy) may be employed to assess product quality.

Profile

The candidate must hold a:

• Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Food Technology, Food Engineering, Food Science, Bioengineering, Biotechnology or a closely related field.

In addition, the candidate should have:

• Excellent academic qualifications.

• Advanced knowledge in food processing.

• Strong communication and writing skills and high self-motivation.

• Openness to interdisciplinary work and a flexible mindset.

• Enthusiasm for engineering, food technology, and sustainability-related questions.

• Expertise in structurization via extrusion, disintegration, or preservation technologies, as well as project management and nutrition, will be considered a plus.

Workplace

We offer

• A multicultural group with a diverse and interdisciplinary team composition.

• Exciting and varied projects in an innovative environment.

• Personal development opportunities through training, teaching, and further education.

• Perspectives for career development.

• A dynamic, collegial working environment with flat hierarchies.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application (English, PDF format), including:

• Motivation letter (max. 1 page) outlining your qualifications and motivation for this project.

• Research proposal (max. 3 pages) on "Future of food processing for affordable, nutritious and more sustainable foods", addressing current challenges, key literature, and innovative approaches.

• CV with list of scientific outputs (e.g., theses, papers).

• Contact details of 2 referees.

• Copies of BSc and MSc diplomas*.

• Copies of BSc and MSc theses (any language)*.

• Transcript listing exams with ECTS credits and grades.

• 1 recommendation letter.

*If you haven’t co

jobs.description:
Doctoral student position – Evaluating novel mineral sources for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Zurich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group in the Department of Health Science and Technology are running a joint strategic research line on Microalgae and plant-based foods in Human Nutrition and Health . The Sustainable Food Processing group focuses on a system-oriented approach in food production via the consideration of the total value chain, including emerging needs in society and their environmental, economic, and social impact. Innovative raw materials are utilized within urban farming and processing concepts to enable new ways of sustainable food supply. The Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism aims to gain insights into the complex relationship between nutrition, metabolism and the epigenome with advanced techniques such as single-cell and next-generation sequencing techniques as well as human and murine in vivo and in vitro studies and combine these with genome-wide computational and bioinformatic analysis. With strong support from these two ETH groups, we are recruiting as soon as possible a talented and highly motivated doctoral student on the topic of ‘Novel sources of minerals for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans’, focusing on investigating the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources in vivo in clinical trials.

Project background

Micronutrient deficiency is a widespread global health problem, primarily driven by inadequate dietary intake. More than 5 billion people are estimated to not consume enough of at least one micronutrient. Among those, mineral deficiencies can be particularly critical, namely, iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium deficiencies, which are particularly common in low- and middle-income countries due to low-mineral diets and primarily affect women and children.

Dietary minerals are typically obtained from a variety of foods including animal-based products such as meat, dairy, and seafood, and plant-based foods such as legumes, cereals, nuts, seeds, and leafy vegetables. However, reliance on conventional animal-based foods raises concerns related to environmental sustainability, ethical considerations, and dietary preferences. Although plant-based foods are generally more sustainable, they often have lower mineral content, bioaccessibility, as well as bioavailability due to the presence of absorption inhibitors such as phytates and polyphenols. Given these limitations, the need exists to explore alternative, more sustainable, and mineral-dense food sources that can effectively address global mineral deficiencies.

Novel mineral sources, such as microalgae, could be a rich source of essential minerals, including iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium, along with proteins, lipids, vitamins, and other bioactive compounds. However, the bioavailability of these minerals needs to be assessed with in vivo clinical trials before large scale application in humans.

Job description

As a doctoral student, you will be responsible for research working towards exploring the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources with clinical trials.

• Summarize the existing knowledge on minerals from novel sources for human nutrition and health

• Design intervention meals (including sensory test) for clinical trials

• Assess the bioaccessibility of minerals in vitro

• Evaluate the mineral bioavailability in vitro

• Carry out clinical trials related to human nutrition enriched with novel mineral sources (key)

• Support teaching activities and co-supervise MSc and BSc students

• Act at the interface between science and technology when supervising students and collaborating with partners from academia and industry

• Support grant applications for the team and support related activities from Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S

descriptionByLocale.it: Descrizione Posizione dottorale degli studenti – Valutazione di nuove fonti minerali per il trattamento delle carenze micronutrienti negli esseri umani 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Laboratorio ETH di Epigenetica, Nutrizione e Metabolismo e Gruppo di Elaborazione Alimentare Sostenibile presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Tecnologie della Salute gestisce una linea di ricerca strategica congiunta su Microalgae e alimenti a base vegetale nella Nutrizione Umana e nella Salute. Il gruppo Sustainable Food Processing si concentra su un approccio orientato al sistema nella produzione alimentare attraverso la considerazione della catena del valore totale, compresi i bisogni emergenti nella società e il loro impatto ambientale, economico e sociale. Le materie prime innovative sono utilizzate all'interno di concetti di agricoltura urbana e di lavorazione per consentire nuove modalità di approvvigionamento alimentare sostenibile. Il Laboratorio di Epigenetica, Nutrizione e Metabolismo si propone di approfondire il complesso rapporto tra nutrizione, metabolismo e epigeno con tecniche avanzate come le tecniche di sequenziamento monocellulare e di prossima generazione, nonché studi umani e murini in vivo e in vitro e combinarli con l'analisi computazionale e bioinformatica a livello genoma. Con il forte sostegno di questi due gruppi ETH, stiamo reclutando il più presto possibile uno studente di dottorato di talento e altamente motivato sul tema “Novel fonti di minerali per il trattamento delle carenze micronutrienti nell’uomo”, concentrandosi sull’indagine sull’assorbimento e la biodisponibilità di nuove fonti minerali in vivo in studi clinici. Sfondo del progetto La carenza di micronutrienti è un problema di salute globale diffuso, principalmente guidato da un'assunzione dietetica insufficiente. Più di 5 miliardi di persone sono stimate di non consumare abbastanza di almeno un micronutriente. Tra questi, le carenze minerali possono essere particolarmente critiche, vale a dire, le carenze di ferro, calcio, zinco e magnesio, che sono particolarmente comuni nei paesi a basso e medio reddito a causa di diete poco minerali e riguardano principalmente donne e bambini. I minerali alimentari sono tipicamente ottenuti da una varietà di alimenti tra cui prodotti a base di animali come carne, latticini e frutti di mare, e alimenti a base vegetale come legumi, cereali, noci, semi e verdure a foglia. Tuttavia, l'affidamento sugli alimenti tradizionali basati sugli animali solleva preoccupazioni relative alla sostenibilità ambientale, considerazioni etiche e preferenze alimentari. Anche se gli alimenti a base vegetale sono generalmente più sostenibili, hanno spesso contenuti minerali più bassi, bioaccessibilità, così come la biodisponibilità a causa della presenza di inibitori di assorbimento come i fiati e i polifenoli. Data queste limitazioni, esiste la necessità di esplorare fonti alimentari alternative, più sostenibili e minerali che possano affrontare efficacemente le carenze minerali globali. Fonti minerali novelli, come le microalghe, potrebbero essere una ricca fonte di minerali essenziali, tra cui ferro, calcio, zinco e magnesio, insieme a proteine, lipidi, vitamine e altri composti bioattivi. Tuttavia, la biodisponibilità di questi minerali deve essere valutata con studi clinici in vivo prima dell'applicazione su larga scala negli esseri umani. descriptionByLocale.en:
Doctoral student position – Evaluating novel mineral sources for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Zurich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group in the Department of Health Science and Technology are running a joint strategic research line on Microalgae and plant-based foods in Human Nutrition and Health . The Sustainable Food Processing group focuses on a system-oriented approach in food production via the consideration of the total value chain, including emerging needs in society and their environmental, economic, and social impact. Innovative raw materials are utilized within urban farming and processing concepts to enable new ways of sustainable food supply. The Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism aims to gain insights into the complex relationship between nutrition, metabolism and the epigenome with advanced techniques such as single-cell and next-generation sequencing techniques as well as human and murine in vivo and in vitro studies and combine these with genome-wide computational and bioinformatic analysis. With strong support from these two ETH groups, we are recruiting as soon as possible a talented and highly motivated doctoral student on the topic of ‘Novel sources of minerals for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans’, focusing on investigating the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources in vivo in clinical trials.

Project background

Micronutrient deficiency is a widespread global health problem, primarily driven by inadequate dietary intake. More than 5 billion people are estimated to not consume enough of at least one micronutrient. Among those, mineral deficiencies can be particularly critical, namely, iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium deficiencies, which are particularly common in low- and middle-income countries due to low-mineral diets and primarily affect women and children.

Dietary minerals are typically obtained from a variety of foods including animal-based products such as meat, dairy, and seafood, and plant-based foods such as legumes, cereals, nuts, seeds, and leafy vegetables. However, reliance on conventional animal-based foods raises concerns related to environmental sustainability, ethical considerations, and dietary preferences. Although plant-based foods are generally more sustainable, they often have lower mineral content, bioaccessibility, as well as bioavailability due to the presence of absorption inhibitors such as phytates and polyphenols. Given these limitations, the need exists to explore alternative, more sustainable, and mineral-dense food sources that can effectively address global mineral deficiencies.

Novel mineral sources, such as microalgae, could be a rich source of essential minerals, including iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium, along with proteins, lipids, vitamins, and other bioactive compounds. However, the bioavailability of these minerals needs to be assessed with in vivo clinical trials before large scale application in humans.

Job description

As a doctoral student, you will be responsible for research working towards exploring the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources with clinical trials.

• Summarize the existing knowledge on minerals from novel sources for human nutrition and health

• Design intervention meals (including sensory test) for clinical trials

• Assess the bioaccessibility of minerals in vitro

• Evaluate the mineral bioavailability in vitro

• Carry out clinical trials related to human nutrition enriched with novel mineral sources (key)

• Support teaching activities and co-supervise MSc and BSc students

• Act at the interface between science and technology when supervising students and collaborating with partners from academia and industry

• Support grant applications for the team and support related activities from Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S

Die Gruppe Sustainable Food Processing konzentriert sich auf einen systemorientierten Ansatz in der Lebensmittelproduktion unter Berücksichtigung der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette, einschließlich der aufstrebenden Bedürfnisse in der Gesellschaft und ihrer ökologischen, wirtschaftlichen und sozialen Auswirkungen. Innovative Rohstoffe werden in städtischen Landwirtschafts- und Verarbeitungskonzepten eingesetzt, um neue Wege der nachhaltigen Lebensmittelversorgung zu ermöglichen. Das Labor für Epigenetik, Ernährung und Metabolismus zielt darauf ab, Einblicke in die komplexe Beziehung zwischen Ernährung, Stoffwechsel und Epigenom mit fortschrittlichen Techniken wie Einzell- und Next-Generation Sequenzierungstechniken sowie menschliche und murine in vivo und in vitro Studien zu gewinnen und diese mit genomweiten rechnerischen und bioinformatischen Analysen zu kombinieren. Mit starker Unterstützung dieser beiden ETH-Gruppen rekrutieren wir so bald wie möglich einen talentierten und hochmotivierten Doktoranden zum Thema „Neue Mineralquellen zur Behandlung von Mikronährstoffmangel beim Menschen“, der sich auf die Untersuchung der Absorption und Bioverfügbarkeit neuartiger Mineralquellen in vivo in klinischen Studien konzentriert. Projekt Hintergrund Mikronährstoffmangel ist ein weit verbreitetes globales Gesundheitsproblem, vor allem durch unzureichende Nahrungsaufnahme angetrieben. Mehr als 5 Milliarden Menschen werden geschätzt, um nicht genug von mindestens einem Mikronährstoff zu konsumieren. Unter diesen können mineralische Mängel besonders kritisch sein, nämlich Eisen-, Kalzium-, Zink- und Magnesiummangel, die besonders häufig in Ländern mit niedrigem und mittlerem Einkommen aufgrund niedrigmineralischer Ernährung und vor allem Frauen und Kinder betreffen. Dietäre Mineralien werden typischerweise aus einer Vielzahl von Lebensmitteln wie Fleisch, Milch und Meeresfrüchten sowie pflanzlichen Lebensmitteln wie Hülsenfrüchten, Getreide, Nüssen, Samen und fruchtigen Gemüsen gewonnen. Die Abhängigkeit von konventionellen tierbasierten Lebensmitteln führt jedoch zu Bedenken im Zusammenhang mit ökologischer Nachhaltigkeit, ethischen Erwägungen und Ernährungspräferenzen. Obwohl pflanzliche Lebensmittel in der Regel nachhaltiger sind, haben sie aufgrund der Anwesenheit von Absorptionsinhibitoren wie Phytate und Polyphenole oft einen geringeren Mineralgehalt, eine Bioverfügbarkeit sowie eine Bioverfügbarkeit. Angesichts dieser Einschränkungen besteht die Notwendigkeit, alternative, nachhaltigere und mineraldichte Lebensmittelquellen zu erforschen, die weltweite Mineralmangel wirksam beheben können. Neuartige Mineralquellen wie Mikroalgen könnten eine reiche Quelle von essentiellen Mineralien sein, einschließlich Eisen, Calcium, Zink und Magnesium, zusammen mit Proteinen, Lipiden, Vitaminen und anderen bioaktiven Verbindungen. Die Bioverfügbarkeit dieser Minerale muss jedoch vor der großtechnischen Anwendung im Menschen mit in vivo klinischen Studien beurteilt werden. Jobbeschreibung Als Doktorandin sind Sie für die Forschung verantwortlich, um die Absorption und Bioverfügbarkeit neuartiger Mineralquellen mit klinischen Studien zu erforschen. - Verbessern Sie das vorhandene Wissen über Mineralien aus neuartigen Quellen für die menschliche Ernährung und Gesundheit - Design Interventionsmehle (einschließlich sensorischer Test) für klinische Studien - Ermöglicht die biologische Zugänglichkeit von Mineralien in vitro - Bewertung der Mineralbioverfügbarkeit in vitro - Durchführung klinischer Studien im Zusammenhang mit der menschlichen Ernährung mit neuartigen Mineralquellen (Schlüssel) - UnterstÃ1⁄4tzung von Lehraktivitäten und Co-Supervise MSc und BSc Studenten - Akt an der Schnittstelle zwischen Wissenschaft und Technologie bei der Betreuung von Studenten und Zusammenarbeit mit Partnern aus Wissenschaft und Industrie - Unterstützungsanträge für das Team und unterstützende Aktivitäten des Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S
descriptionByLocale.fr: Descrizione Position des étudiants au doctorat – Évaluation de nouvelles sources minérales pour le traitement des carences en micronutriments chez l'homme 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Laboratoire d'épigénétique, de nutrition et de métabolisme et le Groupe de la transformation durable des aliments du Département de la science et de la technologie de la santé de Zurich gèrent une ligne de recherche stratégique conjointe sur les microalgues et les aliments à base de plantes dans la nutrition et la santé humaines. Le groupe de la transformation durable des aliments se concentre sur une approche systémique de la production alimentaire en tenant compte de la chaîne de valeur totale, y compris les besoins émergents de la société et leurs incidences environnementales, économiques et sociales. Les matières premières innovantes sont utilisées dans l'agriculture urbaine et les concepts de transformation pour permettre de nouveaux modes d'approvisionnement alimentaire durable. Le Laboratoire d'Epigénétique, de Nutrition et de Métabolisme vise à mieux comprendre la relation complexe entre la nutrition, le métabolisme et l'épigénome avec des techniques avancées telles que les techniques de séquençage monocellulaire et de prochaine génération, ainsi que les études in vivo et in vitro humaines et murines, et à les combiner avec des analyses computationnelles et bio-informatiques à l'échelle du génome. Avec l'appui fort de ces deux groupes d'ETH, nous recrutons dès que possible un doctorant talentueux et très motivé sur le thème «Nouvelles sources de minéraux pour le traitement des carences en micronutriments chez l'humain», en se concentrant sur l'étude de l'absorption et de la biodisponibilité de nouvelles sources minérales in vivo dans les essais cliniques. Contexte du projet La carence en micronutriments est un problème de santé mondial généralisé, principalement dû à une alimentation inadéquate. On estime que plus de 5 milliards de personnes ne consomment pas suffisamment d'au moins un micronutriment. Parmi celles-ci, les carences minérales peuvent être particulièrement critiques, à savoir les carences en fer, en calcium, en zinc et en magnésium, qui sont particulièrement courantes dans les pays à faible revenu et à revenu intermédiaire en raison de régimes à faible revenu minier et touchent principalement les femmes et les enfants. Les minéraux alimentaires sont généralement obtenus à partir de divers aliments, notamment des produits à base d'animaux comme la viande, les produits laitiers et les fruits de mer, et des aliments à base de plantes comme les légumineuses, les céréales, les noix, les graines et les légumes à feuilles. Toutefois, la dépendance à l'égard des aliments traditionnels à base d'animaux soulève des préoccupations liées à la durabilité environnementale, aux considérations éthiques et aux préférences alimentaires. Bien que les aliments à base de plantes soient généralement plus durables, ils ont souvent une teneur minérale inférieure, la bioaccessibilité, ainsi que la biodisponibilité en raison de la présence d'inhibiteurs d'absorption tels que les phytates et les polyphénols. Compte tenu de ces limites, il est nécessaire d'explorer d'autres sources alimentaires, plus durables et plus riches en minéraux, susceptibles de remédier efficacement aux carences minérales mondiales. De nouvelles sources minérales, comme les microalgues, pourraient être une riche source de minéraux essentiels, notamment le fer, le calcium, le zinc et le magnésium, ainsi que des protéines, des lipides, des vitamines et d'autres composés bioactifs. Cependant, la biodisponibilité de ces minéraux doit être évaluée au moyen d'essais cliniques in vivo avant une application à grande échelle chez l' homme. Description du poste En tant qu'étudiant au doctorat, vous serez responsable de la recherche visant à explorer l'absorption et la biodisponibilité de nouvelles sources minérales avec des essais cliniques. - Résumer les connaissances existantes sur les minéraux provenant de sources nouvelles pour la nutrition et la santé humaines - Concevoir des repas d'intervention (y compris des tests sensoriels) pour les essais cliniques - Évaluer la bioaccessibilité des minéraux in vitro - Évaluer la biodisponibilité minérale in vitro - Effectuer des essais cliniques liés à la nutrition humaine enrichie en nouvelles sources minérales (clé) - Soutenir les activités d'enseignement et co-superviser les étudiants en maîtrise et en baccalauréat - Agir à l'interface entre la science et la technologie lors de la supervision des étudiants et de la collaboration avec des partenaires du milieu universitaire et de l'industrie - Demandes de subvention d ' appui à l ' équipe et activités connexes du Centre Singapour-ETH, Centre Bezos

jobs.description:
DevOps Engineer

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the preferred work location is Lugano, but it could also be Zürich.

Project background

We are seeking a versatile and driven DevOps Engineer to help design, build, and operate the software-defined infrastructure and services powering advanced scientific computing and AI/ML workloads at scale.

You will work at the intersection of systems engineering, software engineering, cloud-native infrastructure, and high-performance computing (HPC), contributing to platforms and services used by researchers and engineers tackling complex scientific and AI challenges.

We value strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to learn more than a perfect initial match of technical requirements. We welcome engineers from diverse backgrounds who are eager to contribute and grow. If you are motivated by challenging technical environments and enjoy understanding systems deeply, we strongly encourage you to apply even if your experience does not cover every area listed below.

We are offering a contract initially limited to two years , which will provide the opportunity to contribute to a fast-evolving AI landscape in which CSCS plays a key role and to support high-impact initiatives both nationally and internationally. This includes contributions to the Swiss AI Initiative and similar programs, such as lending support for the development and release of the Apertus models.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Job description

• Design, deploy, automate, and operate scalable infrastructure and cloud-native platform services

• Contribute to Kubernetes-based AI/ML and HPC platforms, including CI/CD, GitOps, observability, security, and operational tooling

• Collaborate with researchers and engineers to support complex workflows, troubleshoot production environments, and improve reliability and performance

• Contribute to platform engineering, automation, and developer productivity initiatives across evolving systems and services

• The technologies and areas below illustrate the breadth of our environment and interests. They are not a checklist of requirements, and experience in only some of these areas is expected

Profile

Technical environment and areas of interest:

• Linux systems engineering, and software development (e.g., Python, Bash)

• Containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitOps, and Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, Helm, Ansible, ArgoCD)

• Distributed systems concepts, APIs, scalability, observability, identity and access management, and security

• AI/ML platforms and supporting infrastructure services

• HPC systems, GPU clusters, and large-scale infrastructure environments

• Platform engineering and developer productivity tooling

• Secure or confidentiality-sensitive operational environments

Personal qualities:

• Curious, hands-on, and eager to understand systems inside-out

• Strong engineering mindset and problem-solving attitude

• Comfortable learning new technologies and working across disciplines

• Effective communicator and collaborative team player

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Experience supporting research or scientific computing environments

• Familiarity with HPC systems and services

• Exposure to GPU clusters and accelerated computing

• Experience with SRE p

jobs.description:
Systems Engineer – Platform Automation

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the work location is Lugano.

Project background

As high-performance computing, AI, and cloud technologies continue to converge; CSCS is redefining how advanced computational services are designed and delivered. Modern scientific and engineering workloads are no longer just large—they are complex, data-intensive, and highly diverse, pushing existing infrastructure to its limits.

We are offering a contract initially limited to two years , which will provide the opportunity to contribute to a fast-evolving AI landscape in which CSCS plays a key role and to support high-impact initiatives both nationally and internationally. This includes contributions to the Swiss AI Initiative and similar programs, such as lending support for the development and release of foundation models in the weather and climate domain.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Job description

The main goal of this position is to develop and manage HPC/AI services on top of a multi-tenant infrastructure. As a Platform automation engineer, you will directly contribute to the design, implementation, maintenance, and documentation of platform services to support HPC and AI. Your work will directly enhance the overall system functionality and efficiency.

Main duties:

• Investigating, troubleshooting, and debugging platform services and infrastructure resources

• Developing, maintaining, and supporting tools and pipelines to support platforms on a geographically redundant infrastructure

• Developing automations to provision, test, deploy, and monitor resources to support the needs of HPC and AI platforms

• Supporting, documenting, and sharing knowledge of tools, and procedur

Profile

You should have a bachelor’s or higher degree in computer engineering, computer science, a relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

You should have a sound knowledge of:

• Experience in the deployment of HPC, AI, or Cloud infrastructures

• Management of HPC/AI services to maximize utilization of compute, storage and high speed network components

• Working knowledge of automation tools and frameworks, including CI/CD processes and ecosystem

• Linux administration skills

Experience with the following is preferred, though there will be ample opportunities to learn and gain more experience with all of these skills on the job:

• Versioning systems and CI/CD workflows such as ArgoCD

• Debugging of microservices running on Kubernetes

• Performance monitoring and diagnostic tools for HPC/AI hardware

• Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform and Ansible

Personal qualities:

• Self-motivated and proactive team player

• Strong communication skills or interest in developing them

• Strong problem-solving mindset with tolerance for uncertainty and change

• Understands user needs and works collaboratively to address them

• Adaptive and willing to learn new technologies with and from others

• Comfortable tackling complex or ambiguous problems

• Comfortable admitting when you don’t know, reaching out and leveraging the right expertise when needed

Project management and methodology:

• Experience with working in self-organized teams

• Familiarity with Agile methodology

• Experience with test-driven development is a plus

Workplace

We offer

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive engineering team and particularly encourage applications from groups underrepres

Il suo laboratorio di utenti è disponibile per i ricercatori nazionali e internazionali in accademia, industria e settore business. Il centro è gestito da ETH Zurich e ha sede presso il suo data center di Lugano e a Zurigo. Per questa posizione la posizione di lavoro è Lugano. I moderni carichi di lavoro scientifici e ingegneristici non sono più solo grandi—sono complessi, intensivi di dati e altamente diversificati, spingendo le infrastrutture esistenti ai suoi limiti. Stiamo offrendo un contratto inizialmente limitato a due anni , che fornirà l'opportunità di contribuire a un paesaggio AI in rapida evoluzione in cui CSCS svolge un ruolo chiave e di sostenere iniziative ad alto impatto sia a livello nazionale che internazionale. Questo include i contributi all'Iniziativa dell'AI svizzera e programmi simili, come il supporto di prestito per lo sviluppo e il rilascio dei modelli di fondazione nel dominio meteo e clima. Il contratto iniziale di due anni potrebbe potenzialmente essere esteso o addirittura diventare permanente. Descrizione del lavoro L'obiettivo principale di questa posizione è quello di sviluppare e gestire i servizi HPC/AI in cima a un'infrastruttura multi-tenant. Come ingegnere di automazione della piattaforma, contribuirai direttamente alla progettazione, implementazione, manutenzione e documentazione dei servizi della piattaforma per supportare HPC e AI. Il vostro lavoro migliorerà direttamente la funzionalità e l'efficienza del sistema generale. Principali doveri:
• Investigazione, risoluzione dei problemi e debug dei servizi della piattaforma e delle risorse infrastrutturali
• Sviluppare, mantenere e supportare strumenti e tubazioni per supportare piattaforme su un'infrastruttura geograficamente ridondante

• Sostenere, documentare e condividere la conoscenza degli strumenti, e procedur Profilo Si dovrebbe avere un diploma di laurea o superiore in ingegneria informatica, informatica, un campo tecnico rilevante, o esperienza pratica equivalente. Si dovrebbe avere una solida conoscenza di:
• Esperienza nella distribuzione delle infrastrutture HPC, AI o Cloud
• Gestione dei servizi HPC/AI per massimizzare l'utilizzo di componenti di calcolo, archiviazione e rete ad alta velocità
• Conoscenze di lavoro di strumenti e quadri di automazione, compresi i processi CI/CD e l'ecosistema
• competenze di amministrazione Linux L'esperienza con il seguente è preferita, anche se ci saranno ampie opportunità per imparare e acquisire più esperienza con tutte queste competenze sul lavoro:
• Sistemi di versione e flussi di lavoro CI/CD come ArgoCD
• Debug di microservizi in esecuzione su Kubernetes
• Monitoraggio delle prestazioni e strumenti diagnostici per l'hardware HPC/AI
• Infrastrutture come strumenti di codice come Terraform e Ansible Qualità personali:
• Giocatore di squadra automotivato e proattivo
• Forte capacità di comunicazione o interesse a svilupparle
• Forte mentalità problem solving con tolleranza per l'incertezza e il cambiamento
• Comprende le esigenze degli utenti e lavora in collaborazione per affrontarli
• Adattativo e disposto ad imparare nuove tecnologie con e da altri
• Confortevoli problemi complessi o ambigui
• Confortevole ammettere quando non si sa, raggiungere e sfruttare la giusta esperienza quando necessario Gestione e metodologia del progetto:
• Esperienza con il lavoro in team auto-organizzati
• Familiarità con la metodologia Agile

• Entwicklung, Aufrechterhaltung und Unterstützung von Werkzeugen und Pipelines zur Unterstützung von Plattformen auf einer geografisch redundanten Infrastruktur

• Erfahrungen bei der Bereitstellung von HPC-, AI- oder Cloud-Infrastrukturen
• Management von HPC/AI-Diensten, um die Nutzung von Rechen-, Speicher- und Hochgeschwindigkeitsnetzkomponenten zu maximieren

jobs.description:
Doktorand:in in Rechtswissenschaften (m/w/d)

100%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

Im Rahmen des SNF-geförderten Projekts „Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary" untersuchen wir gemeinsam mit Schweizer Gerichten, wie künstliche Intelligenz verantwortungsvoll in die Justiz integriert werden kann.

Projekthintergrund

Die Doktorandenstelle ist auf die empirische Erforschung von KI-gestützten Entscheidungshilfen in der Justiz ausgerichtet. Die doktorierende Person wird die Auswirkungen solcher Systeme auf die richterliche Praxis untersuchen – durch die Konzeption und Durchführung von Feldexperimenten in Zusammenarbeit mit Schweizer Gerichten sowie deren rechtliche und institutionelle Evaluation.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Untersuchung richterlicher Entscheidungsprozesse und juristischer Argumentation im Zusammenspiel mit KI-Tools

• Mitwirkung bei der Entwicklung von Experimentdesigns und Evaluierungsrahmen für KI-gestützte Entscheidungsfindung

• Zusammenarbeit mit dem technischen Team zur Erforschung der Interaktion zwischen KI-Systemen und juristischen Nutzern

• Publikation von Forschungsergebnissen in führenden Fachzeitschriften und Präsentation auf internationalen Konferenzen

• Die Stelle ist als kumulative Dissertation an der Schnittstelle von Rechtswissenschaft, Informatik und empirischer Sozialwissenschaft konzipiert

• Unsere Büros befinden sich in der Zürcher Innenstadt

• Die Arbeitssprachen sind Deutsch und Englisch

Profil

• Einen hervorragenden Bachelor- und Masterabschluss in Rechtswissenschaften von einer deutschsprachigen Universität (Deutschland, Österreich oder Schweiz) mitbringen

• Ein ausgeprägtes Interesse an den Auswirkungen von KI auf Recht und Gesellschaft haben

• Interesse an Feldexperimenten und experimentellen Forschungsdesigns mitbringen

• Die Bereitschaft zeigen, quantitative und empirische Forschungsmethoden zu erlernen und anzuwenden

• Über sehr gute Englischkenntnisse verfügen; Deutsch- und Französischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil

Arbeitsort

jobs.description:
PhD position in Multi-State Programmable Robotic Matter

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated PhD student to work on programmable materials that access multiple distinct mechanical states for next-generation robotic matter systems. This 4-year PhD position is fully funded.

Project background

Modern robots increasingly rely on sophisticated mechanisms, such as modular architectures, reconfigurable linkages, deployable structures, and variable-stiffness components, to adapt their bodies to different tasks and environments. However, such adaptability is often achieved by changing geometry, connectivity, or control strategies, while the underlying material properties remain largely fixed.

This project explores a more fundamental route: robotic matter whose constitutive properties can be programmed on demand. By enabling mechanical modulus, viscoelastic response, and flow behavior to be reconfigured within a single continuous body, we aim to move beyond adaptive hardware architectures towards materials that actively participate in robotic function. The long-term vision is to create robots that can tune their physical embodiment through the programmable properties of matter itself.

Job description

• Design, synthesis, and rheological characterization of dynamic covalent polymer composites targeting programmable mechanical state transitions

• Development of theoretical understanding and multiphysics simulation of material behavior across mechanical regimes

• Fabrication and integration of materials into soft robotic demonstrators showcasing multi-state control under external stimuli

• Development of spatial addressability strategies to achieve localized state modulation in a continuous material body

• Demonstration of robotic functions (locomotion, grasping, navigation through constrictions) that exploit multi-state material behavior

• Supervision of bachelor/master students and participation in teaching

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Profile

• MS degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Polymer Chemistry, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields from a leading university

• Strong research track record in one or more of the following: dynamic covalent networks, phase-change materials, rheology of complex materials, stimuli-responsive polymers, or soft robotics

• Enthusiasm for fundamental materials challenges with a drive toward robotic applications

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and comfort with interdisciplinary work spanning chemistry, mechanics, and robotics

• Experience with polymer synthesis, mechanical testing, or material fabrication is a strong plus

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare

descriptionByLocale.it: Posizione di dottorato in Multi-State Programmable Robotic Matter 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Descrizione Il gruppo Robotic Materials sta cercando uno studente di dottorato altamente motivato a lavorare su materiali programmabili che accedono a più stati meccanici distinti per sistemi di materia robotica di prossima generazione. Questa posizione PhD di 4 anni è completamente finanziata. Progetto di sfondo I robot moderni si affidano sempre più a meccanismi sofisticati, come le architetture modulari, i collegamenti riconfigurabili, le strutture dispiegabili e i componenti a variabili, per adattare i loro corpi a diversi compiti e ambienti. Tuttavia, tale adattabilità è spesso raggiunta cambiando la geometria, la connettività o le strategie di controllo, mentre le proprietà dei materiali sottostanti rimangono in gran parte fissate. Questo progetto esplora un percorso più fondamentale: la materia robotica le cui proprietà costitutive possono essere programmate a richiesta. Con l'attivazione del modulo meccanico, della risposta viscoelastica e del comportamento del flusso da riconfigurare all'interno di un unico corpo continuo, ci proponiamo di andare oltre le architetture hardware adattative verso materiali che partecipano attivamente alla funzione robotica. La visione a lungo termine è quella di creare robot in grado di sintonizzare la loro incarnazione fisica attraverso le proprietà programmabili della materia stessa. Descrizione del lavoro - Progettazione, sintesi e caratterizzazione reologica dei compositi polimeri covalenti dinamici che mirano alle transizioni di stato meccanico programmabili - Sviluppo della comprensione teorica e simulazione multifisica del comportamento materiale attraverso i regimi meccanici - La fabbricazione e l'integrazione dei materiali in morbidi dimostranti robotizzati che mostrano il controllo multi-stato sotto stimoli esterni - Sviluppo di strategie di indirizzabilità spaziale per raggiungere modulazione di stato localizzata in un corpo materiale continuo - Dimostrazione delle funzioni robotiche (locomozione, presa, navigazione attraverso costrizioni) che sfruttano il comportamento materiale multi-stato - Supervisione degli studenti di laurea/master e partecipazione all'insegnamento Profilo - Laurea in Scienze e Ingegneria dei Materiali, Chimica Polimeri, Ingegneria Meccanica, o campi correlati da un'università leader - Forte tracciato di ricerca in una o più delle seguenti: reti covalenti dinamiche, materiali a cambio di fase, reologia di materiali complessi, polimeri a risposta stimolante, o robotica morbida - Enthusiasm per le sfide materiali fondamentali con una spinta verso applicazioni robotiche - Eccellente capacità di problem solving e comfort con lavoro interdisciplinare che spazia la chimica, la meccanica e la robotica - L'esperienza con sintesi polimerica, collaudo meccanico o fabbricazione di materiale è un forte plus Lavoro - Un ambiente di lavoro produttivo con formazione e guida dal PI regolarmente - stipendio competitivo secondo gli standard ETH (situazione a tempo pieno, a termine fisso) - Un team interdisciplinare, internazionale e diversificato di talenti e un gruppo stimolante, vibrante e collaborativo - forti connessioni con partner accademici, industriali e clinici nella scienza dei materiali, nella robotica e nella sanità Contatto chevron right Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca presso l'ETH di Zurigo - Valiamo la diversità e la sostenibilità - In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, la diversità di valore e nutrire un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutto il nostro staff e gli studenti sono rispettati. Visita il nostro sito Equal Opportunities and Diversity per scoprire come garantiamo un ambiente equo e aperto che permetta a tutti di crescere e fiorire. - La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi – stiamo lavorando costantemente verso un futuro neutro dal clima. descriptionByLocale.fr: Poste de doctorat en matière robotique programmable multi-États 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Descrizione Le groupe des matériaux robotiques recherche un doctorant très motivé pour travailler sur des matériaux programmables qui accèdent à de multiples états mécaniques distincts pour les systèmes robotiques de nouvelle génération. Ce poste de doctorat de 4 ans est entièrement financé. Progetto di fond Les robots modernes s'appuient de plus en plus sur des mécanismes sophistiqués, tels que des architectures modulaires, des liens reconfigurables, des structures déployables et des composants à coupe variable, pour adapter leur corps à différentes tâches et environnements. Cependant, une telle adaptabilité est souvent obtenue en modifiant la géométrie, la connectivité ou les stratégies de contrôle, alors que les propriétés matérielles sous-jacentes restent largement fixes. Ce projet explore une voie plus fondamentale : la robotique dont les propriétés constitutives peuvent être programmées sur demande. En permettant la reconfiguration du module mécanique, de la réponse viscoélastique et du comportement d'écoulement au sein d'un seul corps continu, nous visons à dépasser les architectures matérielles adaptatives vers des matériaux qui participent activement à la fonction robotique. La vision à long terme est de créer des robots qui peuvent ajuster leur incarnation physique à travers les propriétés programmables de la matière elle-même. Descrizione del lavoro - Conception, synthèse et caractérisation rhéologique de composites de polymères covalents dynamiques ciblant les transitions mécaniques programmables - Développement de la compréhension théorique et simulation multiphysique du comportement matériel à travers les régimes mécaniques - Fabrication et intégration de matériaux dans des démonstrateurs robotiques souples montrant un contrôle multi-états sous stimuli externes - Élaboration de stratégies d'adressabilité spatiale pour obtenir une modulation d'état localisée dans un corps matériel continu - Démonstration de fonctions robotiques (locomotion, saisie, navigation par constrictions) qui exploitent le comportement matériel multiétat - Supervision des bacheliers/maîtrises et participation à l'enseignement Profil - Maîtrise en sciences des matériaux et génie, chimie des polymères, génie mécanique ou domaines connexes d'une université de premier plan - Forts résultats de recherche dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : réseaux covalents dynamiques, matériaux de changement de phase, rhéologie de matériaux complexes, polymères sensibles aux stimuli ou robotique douce - Enthousiasme pour les défis fondamentaux des matériaux avec un élan vers les applications robotiques - Excellente capacité de résolution de problèmes et confort avec des travaux interdisciplinaires couvrant la chimie, la mécanique et la robotique - L'expérience de la synthèse des polymères, des essais mécaniques ou de la fabrication de matériaux est un plus fort Lavoro - Un environnement de travail productif avec une formation et des conseils réguliers de l'IP - The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Training Network COMBINE brings together 17 academic institutions and 14 industrial partners across Europe.The network addresses key challenges in fluid structure interaction (FSI) relevant to energy, process, and materials engineering, with a strong focus on:

• Advanced numerical modelling and simulation

• la modélisation numérique avancée et la simulation
• les méthodes expérimentales et les technologies de capteurs

• Construction d'une installation avec une seule tige et un faisceau de tiges

Postdoctoral Researcher in Light-Driven CO2 Capture

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Electrochemical Energy Systems Laboratory in the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering at ETH Zurich invites applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position focused on light-driven CO2 capture.

Job description

• Our group is actively developing a novel photoacid-based approach for efficient CO2 capture, optimizing both the local chemical environment in photoacids and their molecular structure to enhance sorption capacity and stability

• We seek a postdoctoral researcher who will contribute to these efforts

• You will join a diverse, inclusive, and supportive work environment that values scientific curiosity and creativity

Profile

• PhD in Physical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Material Science, or a related field

• Experience with in situ spectroscopy is a plus

• Excellent written and spoken English

• Self-driven, highly motivated, and strong teamwork skills

We welcome applications from candidates with expertise in organic synthesis and one or more of the following areas:

• Photochemistry

• Advanced characterization techniques (e.g., synchrotron facilities, in-situ methods)

• CO2 capture / utilization is a plus

We are looking for highly motivated researchers with a passion for contributing to solutions in the global energy landscape. If you excel in collaborative environments and can bring expertise in some of the areas listed above, we encourage you to apply.

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

jobs.description:
PhD position in Computational earthquake rupture mechanics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

At the Professorship of Solid Mechanics (SMEC) in the Institute for Building Materials at ETH Zurich, we aim to understand how materials deform, degrade, break, and ultimately fail. Our research is driven by curiosity about the physical mechanisms that underlie failure and by the ambition to translate this understanding into more reliable and resilient materials and structures. By combining numerical modeling, laboratory experiments, and theoretical analyses, we seek to link microscopic processes with the macroscopic behavior of both engineering and natural systems and develop predictive tools for mechanical failure.

Our team is highly interdisciplinary and international, bringing together researchers with backgrounds in materials science, mechanics, and applied physics. We work across a broad range of topics, including the mechanics of particle systems (colloidal and granular), architected and topologically interlocked materials, the mechanics of fragility in collagen, the mechanics of earthquakes, fracture of soft materials, and modeling failure in multiphysical processes such as corrosion-driven degradation of concrete. What unites these efforts is a shared curiosity about why complex materials fail and a commitment to developing new concepts, experiments, and models that advance our understanding of failure mechanics.

We are seeking a motivated, innovative PhD student with a background in computational mechanics to work on a project in computational earthquake rupture mechanics. The project will combine numerical method development and theoretical analysis to investigate how heterogeneous stress states and nonlinear near-fault processes influence earthquake rupture propagation, arrest, and earthquake-size statistics.

Job description

• You will conduct a computational and theoretical investigation of dynamic earthquake rupture, with a focus on rupture propagation, rupture arrest, and energy dissipation in heterogeneous fault systems

• The work will connect fracture-mechanics theory with large-scale numerical simulations of earthquake rupture

• You will develop, improve, and use high-performance simulation tools for dynamic rupture, including GPU-oriented numerical methods

• You will verify and validate the numerical methods against benchmark problems and established theoretical results

• Building on these tools, you will investigate how heterogeneous stress states and nonlinear dissipative processes, such as off-fault plasticity, influence rupture arrest and earthquake-size statistics

• The position provides a stimulating environment for scientific growth and collaboration

Profile

• You hold an MSc degree in mechanics, physics, engineering, earth science, material science, computational science, or a related discipline

• You have a background in computational mechanics, solid mechanics, applied physics, scientific computing, or a related field

• You have experience implementing scientific code and validating it against analytical solutions, numerical benchmarks, or well-documented reference results.

• You have prior programming experience in Python and have used version control. Experience with high-performance computing, GPU programming, C/C++, or numerical methods for wave propagation, fracture, or solid mechanics is an advantage

• You are curious, self-motivated, and enjoy developing numerical methods to answer mechanics questions

• You are fluent in English, both oral and written

• You enjoy working in a team, possess the necessary social skills and communication abilities, and contribute proactively to a positive group atmosphere

Workplace

We offer

• You will join a dynamic, international, and supportive research group that values curiosity, rigor, and collaboration.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Descrizione Alla cattedra di Meccanica dei Solidi (SMEC) presso l'Istituto dei Materiali da Costruzione dell'ETH di Zurigo, miriamo a capire come i materiali si deformano, si degradano, si rompono e, infine, si guastano. La nostra ricerca è guidata dalla curiosità verso i meccanismi fisici che sono alla base dei cedimenti e dall’ambizione di tradurre questa comprensione in materiali e strutture più affidabili e resilienti. Combinando modellazione numerica, esperimenti di laboratorio e analisi teoriche, cerchiamo di collegare i processi microscopici con il comportamento macroscopico sia dei sistemi ingegneristici che naturali e di sviluppare strumenti predittivi per i guasti meccanici. Il nostro team è altamente interdisciplinare e internazionale e riunisce ricercatori con background in scienza dei materiali, meccanica e fisica applicata. Lavoriamo su un'ampia gamma di argomenti, tra cui la meccanica dei sistemi di particelle (colloidali e granulari), materiali strutturati e topologicamente interconnessi, la meccanica della fragilità del collagene, la meccanica dei terremoti, la frattura di materiali morbidi e la modellazione dei guasti in processi multifisici come il degrado del calcestruzzo causato dalla corrosione. Ciò che unisce questi sforzi è una curiosità condivisa sul perché i materiali complessi falliscono e l’impegno nello sviluppo di nuovi concetti, esperimenti e modelli che migliorino la nostra comprensione dei meccanismi dei guasti.
• Cerchiamo uno studente di dottorato motivato e innovativo con un background in meccanica computazionale per lavorare su un progetto sulla meccanica computazionale della rottura dei terremoti. Il progetto combinerà lo sviluppo di metodi numerici e l’analisi teorica per studiare come gli stati di stress eterogenei e i processi non lineari di quasi faglia influenzano la propagazione della rottura del terremoto, l’arresto e le statistiche sulle dimensioni del terremoto. Descrizione del lavoro - Condurre un'indagine computazionale e teorica sulla rottura dinamica del terremoto, con particolare attenzione alla propagazione della rottura, all'arresto della rottura e alla dissipazione di energia in sistemi di faglie eterogenei - Collegare la teoria della meccanica della frattura con simulazioni numeriche su larga scala della rottura del terremoto - Sviluppare, migliorare e utilizzare strumenti di simulazione ad alte prestazioni per la rottura dinamica, inclusi metodi numerici orientati alla GPU - Verificare e convalidare i metodi numerici rispetto a problemi di riferimento e risultati teorici consolidati - Investigare come gli stati di stress eterogenei e processi dissipativi non lineari, come plasticità fuori faglia, arresto di rottura e statistiche sulle dimensioni dei terremoti - Fornire un ambiente stimolante per la crescita scientifica e la collaborazione Profilo - Possedere un master in meccanica, fisica, ingegneria, scienze della terra, scienza dei materiali, scienze computazionali o una disciplina correlata - Avere esperienza in meccanica computazionale, meccanica dei solidi, fisica applicata, informatica scientifica o un campo correlato - Avere esperienza nell'implementazione di codice scientifico e nella sua convalida rispetto a soluzioni analitiche, benchmark numerici o risultati di riferimento ben documentati - Avere esperienza di programmazione precedente in Python e hanno utilizzato il controllo della versione. L'esperienza con il calcolo ad alte prestazioni, la programmazione GPU, C/C++ o metodi numerici per la propagazione delle onde, la frattura o la meccanica dei solidi costituisce un vantaggio - Essere curioso, automotivato e divertirsi nello sviluppo di metodi numerici per rispondere a domande di meccanica - Essere fluente in inglese, sia orale che scritto - Piacere lavorare in gruppo, possedere le necessarie abilità sociali e comunicative e contribuire in modo proattivo a un'atmosfera di gruppo positiva Cosa offerta - Partecipa a un gruppo di ricerca dinamico, internazionale e solidale che valorizza la curiosità, il rigore e la collaborazione - Il tuo lavoro ha un impatto: diventa parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo sostiene il tuo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce anche attivamente alla tua crescita professionale e al tuo successo

descriptionByLocale.de: Beschreibung: An der Professur für Festkörpermechanik (SMEC) am Institut für Baustoffe der ETH Zürich wollen wir verstehen, wie sich Materialien verformen, zersetzen, brechen und letztendlich versagen. Unsere Forschung basiert auf der Neugier auf die physikalischen Mechanismen, die einem Versagen zugrunde liegen, und dem Ehrgeiz, dieses Verständnis in zuverlässigere und widerstandsfähigere Materialien und Strukturen umzusetzen. Durch die Kombination numerischer Modellierung, Laborexperimente und theoretischer Analysen versuchen wir, mikroskopische Prozesse mit dem makroskopischen Verhalten sowohl technischer als auch natürlicher Systeme zu verknüpfen und Vorhersagewerkzeuge für mechanisches Versagen zu entwickeln. Unser Team ist äußerst interdisziplinär und international und vereint Forscher mit Hintergrund in den Materialwissenschaften, der Mechanik und der angewandten Physik. Wir arbeiten zu einem breiten Themenspektrum, darunter die Mechanik von Partikelsystemen (kolloidal und körnig), architektonische und topologisch ineinandergreifende Materialien, die Mechanik der Zerbrechlichkeit von Kollagen, die Mechanik von Erdbeben, den Bruch weicher Materialien und die Modellierung von Fehlern in multiphysikalischen Prozessen wie der korrosionsbedingten Zersetzung von Beton. Was diese Bemühungen vereint, ist die gemeinsame Neugier, warum komplexe Materialien versagen, und das Engagement für die Entwicklung neuer Konzepte, Experimente und Modelle, die unser Verständnis der Versagensmechanik verbessern. Wir suchen einen motivierten, innovativen Doktoranden mit einem Hintergrund in computergestützter Mechanik, der an einem Projekt zur rechnergestützten Erdbeben-Bruchmechanik arbeitet. Das Projekt wird die Entwicklung numerischer Methoden und theoretische Analysen kombinieren, um zu untersuchen, wie heterogene Spannungszustände und nichtlineare fehlernahe Prozesse die Ausbreitung, den Stillstand und die Erdbebengrößenstatistik von Erdbebenbrüchen beeinflussen. Stellenbeschreibung - Führen Sie eine rechnerische und theoretische Untersuchung des dynamischen Erdbebenbruchs durch, mit Schwerpunkt auf Bruchausbreitung, Bruchstopp und Energiedissipation in heterogenen Verwerfungssystemen. - Verbinden Sie die Theorie der Bruchmechanik mit groß angelegten numerischen Simulationen des Erdbebenbruchs nichtlineare dissipative Prozesse wie Off-Fault-Plastizität, Influencer-Rupture-Arrest und Erdbebengrößenstatistiken - Bieten Sie ein stimulierendes Umfeld für wissenschaftliches Wachstum und Zusammenarbeit. Erfahrung mit Hochleistungsrechnen, GPU-Programmierung, C/C++ oder numerischen Methoden für Wellenausbreitung, Bruch oder Festkörpermechanik ist von Vorteil. - Seien Sie neugierig, selbstmotiviert und haben Freude an der Entwicklung numerischer Methoden zur Beantwortung mechanischer Fragen. - Sie sprechen fließend Englisch, sowohl mündlich als auch schriftlich. - Sie haben Spaß an der Arbeit im Team, verfügen über die notwendigen sozialen Kompetenzen und Kommunikationsfähigkeiten und tragen proaktiv zu einer positiven Gruppenatmosphäre bei. descriptionByLocale.fr: Description À la Chaire de mécanique des solides (SMEC) de l'Institut des matériaux de construction de l'ETH Zurich, notre objectif est de comprendre comment les matériaux se déforment, se dégradent, se brisent et finissent par échouer. Nos recherches sont motivées par la curiosité pour les mécanismes physiques qui sont à l’origine de l’échec et par l’ambition de traduire cette compréhension en matériaux et structures plus fiables et plus résilients. En combinant modélisation numérique, expériences en laboratoire et analyses théoriques, nous cherchons à relier les processus microscopiques au comportement macroscopique des systèmes techniques et naturels et à développer des outils prédictifs des défaillances mécaniques. Notre équipe est hautement interdisciplinaire et internationale, réunissant des chercheurs issus de la science des matériaux, de la mécanique et de la physique appliquée. Nous travaillons sur un large éventail de sujets, notamment la mécanique des systèmes de particules (colloïdaux et granulaires), les matériaux architecturés et topologiquement imbriqués, la mécanique de la fragilité du collagène, la mécanique des tremblements de terre, la fracture des matériaux mous et la modélisation des défaillances dans des processus multiphysiques tels que la dégradation du béton provoquée par la corrosion. Ce qui unit ces efforts est une curiosité commune quant aux raisons pour lesquelles des matériaux complexes échouent et un engagement à développer de nouveaux concepts, expériences et modèles qui font progresser notre compréhension de la mécanique de la défaillance. Nous recherchons un doctorant motivé et innovant avec une formation en mécanique computationnelle pour travailler sur un projet en mécanique computationnelle de rupture sismique. Le projet combinera le développement de méthodes numériques et l'analyse théorique pour étudier comment les états de contraintes hétérogènes et les processus non linéaires proches de la faille influencent la propagation, l'arrêt et les statistiques de l'ampleur des séismes. Description du poste - Mener une étude informatique et théorique de la rupture sismique dynamique, en mettant l'accent sur la propagation de la rupture, l'arrêt de la rupture et la dissipation d'énergie dans les systèmes de failles hétérogènes - Relier la théorie de la mécanique des fractures aux simulations numériques à grande échelle de la rupture sismique - Développer, améliorer et utiliser des outils de simulation haute performance pour la rupture dynamique, y compris les méthodes numériques orientées GPU - Vérifier et valider les méthodes numériques par rapport à des problèmes de référence et aux résultats théoriques établis - Étudier comment les états de contrainte hétérogènes et les processus de dissipation non linéaires, tels que hors défaut - Avoir une formation en mécanique computationnelle, en mécanique des solides, en physique appliquée, en calcul scientifique ou dans un domaine connexe - Avoir une expérience dans la mise en œuvre de code scientifique et sa validation par rapport à des solutions analytiques, des références numériques ou des résultats de référence bien documentés - Avoir une expérience préalable en programmation en Python et avoir utilisé le contrôle de version. Une expérience en calcul haute performance, en programmation GPU, en C/C++ ou en méthodes numériques pour la propagation des ondes, la fracture ou la mécanique des solides est un avantage. - Être curieux, motivé et aimer développer des méthodes numériques pour répondre à des questions de mécanique. - Parler couramment l'anglais, à l'oral et à l'écrit. - Aimer travailler en équipe, posséder les compétences sociales et de communication nécessaires et contribuer de manière proactive à une atmosphère de groupe positive. impact : faites partie de l'ETH Zurich, qui non seulement soutient votre développement professionnel, mais contribue également activement à votre croissance et à votre réussite professionnelle.

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We invite applications for a PhD position at the intersection of quantum computing and artificial intelligence, focused on the challenge of advancing optimization through both technologies. The position is jointly in collaboration with Stefan Woerner (Principal Research Scientist & Manager, Applied Quantum Science, IBM Research Europe – Zurich) and by Juan Carrasquilla (Institute for Theoretical Physics, Department of Physics, ETH Zurich).

Job description

You will have the opportunity to work across both ETH Zurich and IBM Research Zurich, benefiting from the synergy between academic and industrial research. The topic of the PhD position sits at the crossroads of quantum computing, machine learning, and combinatorial optimization — an area where some of the most exciting and open questions in the field live. Research directions include:

• Using AI to learn parameters and design circuits for quantum optimization algorithms (e.g., beyond QUBO formulations for QAOA)

• Developing AI-driven methods to discover quantum optimization algorithms

• Generating quantum samples to warm-start classical AI solvers, or to produce quantum-enhanced features and embeddings

The core questions driving this research are fundamental and timely: How can we ensure AI-discovered quantum algorithms are not classical in disguise? How can we generate large-scale, high-quality quantum training data? And how can we combine quantum computing and AI to achieve a measurable, real-world advantage?

Profile

• A Masters degree in physics, mathematics, applied mathematics, computer science, quantum computing, machine learning

• Strong interest in the development of theoretical or computational methods for optimization methods, quantum computing, and machine learning

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher in Multimodal Reasoning Models for Oncology

100%, Basel, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We are seeking an exceptional and highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to lead research on multimodal reasoning models for oncology. The project focuses on developing, post-training, and evaluating flexible AI models that can support complex oncologic diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making in a safe, transparent, and clinically grounded manner.

The successful candidate will work on oncology-focused multimodal reasoning models that combine language, vision, biomedical knowledge, clinical context, and relevant patient-level data to produce reliable, auditable, and uncertainty-aware outputs.

A major focus of the position is the development of AI-based reasoning strategies for oncology, including tool-augmented inference, multi-agent or compound model workflows, process supervision, verifier-guided training, and reinforcement learning-based post-training. The goal is to build systems that can justify recommendations, cite supporting evidence, calibrate uncertainty, defer appropriately, and operate safely in clinically realistic settings.

This position is embedded within a highly interdisciplinary collaboration between ETH Zurich, Kaiko.ai, and clinical partners, offering an opportunity to advance foundational AI research while working toward real-world translation in oncology.

Job description

Reasoning Models for Oncology

Development and adaptation of oncology-focused foundation models capable of reasoning over complex clinical questions, including diagnosis, molecular interpretation, treatment selection, and longitudinal care.

This may include:

• Multimodal language model architectures

• Integration of clinical context, biomedical literature, guidelines, and patient-level multimodal evidence

• Adaptation and evaluation on public and institutional oncology datasets

• Development of uncertainty-aware and safety-aware reasoning behavior

Reasoning Strategies, Agents, and Tool Use

Development of model workflows that can use external tools and knowledge sources in a reliable and auditable way.

Examples include:

• Retrieval from literature, clinical guidelines, and trial databases

• Clinical trial matching and therapy evidence lookup

• Variant interpretation and molecular knowledgebase use

• Multi-agent systems for decomposing complex oncology tasks into hierarchical context streams

• Citation-grounded and traceable outputs suitable for expert review

Process Supervision and Post-Training

Development of post-training methods that improve clinical reasoning quality, reliability, and safety.

• Process-level supervision for intermediate reasoning steps

• Outcome-based supervision using expert or guideline-derived signals

• Reinforcement learning for oncology-specific reasoning behavior

• Comparison and development of RL training approaches

• Calibration, abstention, and safety-aware optimization

Clinical Evaluation and Safety

Evaluation of oncology reasoning models in clinically meaningful settings.

Key evaluation dimensions include:

• Guideline concordance

• Diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning quality

• Molecular interpretation accuracy

• Tool-use reliability

• Citation quality and evidence grounding

• Calibration, uncertainty, and appropriate deferral

• Trace auditability and clinician-in-the-loop evaluation

Profile

Must Have

• PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Medical AI, Biomedical Informatics, Computational Biology, or a related field

• Strong programming skills in Python and modern ML frameworks

• Experience with deep learning and large language models

• Strong publication record in AI/ML, medical AI, computational biology, biomedical informatics, or related areas

• Ability to work in highly interdisciplinary research environments

Preferred

• Experience with foundation models, multimodal models, or biomedical/clinical language models

• Experience

descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral Researcher in Multimodal Reasoning Models for Oncology

100%, Basel, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We are seeking an exceptional and highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to lead research on multimodal reasoning models for oncology. The project focuses on developing, post-training, and evaluating flexible AI models that can support complex oncologic diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making in a safe, transparent, and clinically grounded manner.

The successful candidate will work on oncology-focused multimodal reasoning models that combine language, vision, biomedical knowledge, clinical context, and relevant patient-level data to produce reliable, auditable, and uncertainty-aware outputs.

A major focus of the position is the development of AI-based reasoning strategies for oncology, including tool-augmented inference, multi-agent or compound model workflows, process supervision, verifier-guided training, and reinforcement learning-based post-training. The goal is to build systems that can justify recommendations, cite supporting evidence, calibrate uncertainty, defer appropriately, and operate safely in clinically realistic settings.

This position is embedded within a highly interdisciplinary collaboration between ETH Zurich, Kaiko.ai, and clinical partners, offering an opportunity to advance foundational AI research while working toward real-world translation in oncology.

Job description

Reasoning Models for Oncology

Development and adaptation of oncology-focused foundation models capable of reasoning over complex clinical questions, including diagnosis, molecular interpretation, treatment selection, and longitudinal care.

This may include:

• Multimodal language model architectures

• Integration of clinical context, biomedical literature, guidelines, and patient-level multimodal evidence

• Adaptation and evaluation on public and institutional oncology datasets

• Development of uncertainty-aware and safety-aware reasoning behavior

Reasoning Strategies, Agents, and Tool Use

Development of model workflows that can use external tools and knowledge sources in a reliable and auditable way.

Examples include:

• Retrieval from literature, clinical guidelines, and trial databases

• Clinical trial matching and therapy evidence lookup

• Variant interpretation and molecular knowledgebase use

• Multi-agent systems for decomposing complex oncology tasks into hierarchical context streams

• Citation-grounded and traceable outputs suitable for expert review

Process Supervision and Post-Training

Development of post-training methods that improve clinical reasoning quality, reliability, and safety.

• Process-level supervision for intermediate reasoning steps

• Outcome-based supervision using expert or guideline-derived signals

• Reinforcement learning for oncology-specific reasoning behavior

• Comparison and development of RL training approaches

• Calibration, abstention, and safety-aware optimization

Clinical Evaluation and Safety

Evaluation of oncology reasoning models in clinically meaningful settings.

Key evaluation dimensions include:

• Guideline concordance

• Diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning quality

• Molecular interpretation accuracy

• Tool-use reliability

• Citation quality and evidence grounding

• Calibration, uncertainty, and appropriate deferral

• Trace auditability and clinician-in-the-loop evaluation

Profile

Must Have

• PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Medical AI, Biomedical Informatics, Computational Biology, or a related field

• Strong programming skills in Python and modern ML frameworks

• Experience with deep learning and large language models

• Strong publication record in AI/ML, medical AI, computational biology, biomedical informatics, or related areas

• Ability to work in highly interdisciplinary research environments

Preferred

• Experience with foundation models, multimodal models, or biomedical/clinical language models

• Experience

Architekt:in / Teilprojektleiter:in Planung (m/w/d)

80%-100%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

Die ETH Zürich startet mit dem «Living Lab HIL» ein pionierhaftes Forschungsprojekt mit direktem Bezug zur Baupraxis. Das HIL-Gebäude auf dem Campus Hönggerberg wird zu einem Reallabor. Der sanierungsbedürftige Bau wird umgebaut und erweitert. In den kommenden Jahren erforschen und planen Professuren der Departemente Architektur (D-ARCH) sowie Bau, Umwelt und Geomatik (D-BAUG) die Sanierung des Gebäudes HIL im Sinne des zirkulären Bauens. Ziel ist es, das nachhaltige Entwerfen und Bauen im Bestand weiterzuentwickeln und exemplarisch an einem realen Planungs- und Bauprojekt anzuwenden.

Für das Planungsteam des Living Lab HIL suchen wir eine erfahrene Architektin oder einen erfahrenen Architekten, der unsere komplexen und anspruchsvollen Teilprojekte eigenverantwortlich plant, koordiniert und baulich umsetzt – von der Sanierung des Bestandes über die Aufstockung des HIL-Gebäudes bis hin zur Entwicklung innovativer Makerspaces. Sie begleiten die Projekte über alle Phasen hinweg und decken das gesamte Spektrum von der Planung bis zur Realisierung vor Ort ab.

Stellenbeschreibung

In dieser projektbezogenen Rolle übernehmen Sie schwerpunktmässig folgende Aufgaben und Verantwortungen:

• Teilprojektleitung: Eigenverantwortliche Führung, Koordination und Umsetzung spezifischer Teilprojekte (z. B. Sanierung im laufenden Betrieb, innovative Aufstockung).

• SIA-Phasen 1–5: Vollständige Bearbeitung und Steuerung der Projekte über alle SIA-Leistungsphasen hinweg, von der Vorstudie bis zur erfolgreichen Ausführung und Inbetriebnahme.

• Prototypische Umsetzung: Detail- und Ausführungsplanung von hochinnovativen, zirkulären und prototypischen Baukonstruktionen in direkter Zusammenarbeit mit beteiligten Professuren.

• Projektcontrolling: Strikte Verantwortung für die Einhaltung von Terminen, Qualitäten und Kosten innerhalb der Budgets und Abläufe der ETH Real Estate.

• Schnittstellenführung: Enger Austausch und Abstimmung mit Unternehmern, Behörden, Fachplanern sowie Vertretern aus Lehre und Forschung.

• Die Stelle ist vorerst auf maximal fünf Jahre befristet, zunächst mit einem Einjahresvertrag mit Verlängerungsoptionen.

Profil

Um die Anforderungen dieser anspruchsvollen Position ideal zu erfüllen, bringen Sie folgendes Profil mit:

• Ausbildung: Abgeschlossenes Studium in Architektur (ETH/FH oder gleichwertig).

• Berufserfahrung: Fundierte, mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Ausführungsplanung und Projektkoordination in der Schweiz. Nachweisbare Erfahrung über alle SIA-Phasen ist zwingend erforderlich.

• Fachkenntnisse: Hervorragende Kenntnisse der Schweizer Bauvorschriften, Normen (SIA) und Bewilligungsverfahren, idealerweise mit Erfahrung im Bauen im Bestand.

• CAD-Kenntnisse: Sehr gute, praxiserprobte Kenntnisse in 3D-CAD, vorzugsweise Rhino und VisualArq oder vergleichbaren BIM-Systemen.

• Persönlichkeit: Strukturierte, selbständige Arbeitsweise, ausgeprägtes Verantwortungsbewusstsein, Flexibilität und Freude an unkonventionellen, innovativen Baulösungen.

• Sprachen: Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sowie gute Englischkenntnisse.

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

• Abwechslungsreiche Projektbearbeitung an der Schnittstelle von Architektur, Forschung und Praxis.

• Ihr Arbeitsort ist im neuen Projektbüro im HIL-Gebäude auf dem ETH-Campus Hönggerberg.

• Ihre Position ist dem Projektteam im Departement Architektur angegliedert.

• Wir bieten attraktive Arbeitsbedingungen in einem dynamischen, innovativen und internationalen Umfeld.

• Sie arbeiten eigenverantwortlich und in ständigem kollegialem Austausch mit unserem Team und einer Vielfalt an Partner:innen und Anspruchsgruppen.
