In den kommenden Jahren erforschen und planen Professuren der Departemente Architektur (D-ARCH) sowie Bau, Umwelt und Geomatik (D-BAUG) die Sanierung des Gebäudes HIL im Sinne des zirkulären Bauens. Ziel ist es, das nachhaltige Entwerfen und Bauen im Bestand weiterzuentwickeln und exemplarisch an einem realen Planungs- und Bauprojekt anzuwenden.

Für das Planungsteam des Living Lab HIL suchen wir eine erfahrene Architektin oder einen erfahrenen Architekten, der unsere komplexen und anspruchsvollen Teilprojekte eigenverantwortlich plant, koordiniert und baulich umsetzt – von der Sanierung des Bestandes über die Aufstockung des HIL-Gebäudes bis hin zur Entwicklung innovativer Makerspaces. Sie begleiten die Projekte über alle Phasen hinweg und decken das gesamte Spektrum von der Planung bis zur Realisierung vor Ort ab.

Stellenbeschreibung

In dieser projektbezogenen Rolle übernehmen Sie schwerpunktmässig folgende Aufgaben und Verantwortungen:

• Teilprojektleitung: Eigenverantwortliche Führung, Koordination und Umsetzung spezifischer Teilprojekte (z. B. Sanierung im laufenden Betrieb, innovative Aufstockung).

• SIA-Phasen 1–5: Vollständige Bearbeitung und Steuerung der Projekte über alle SIA-Leistungsphasen hinweg, von der Vorstudie bis zur erfolgreichen Ausführung und Inbetriebnahme.

• Prototypische Umsetzung: Detail- und Ausführungsplanung von hochinnovativen, zirkulären und prototypischen Baukonstruktionen in direkter Zusammenarbeit mit beteiligten Professuren.

• Projektcontrolling: Strikte Verantwortung für die Einhaltung von Terminen, Qualitäten und Kosten innerhalb der Budgets und Abläufe der ETH Real Estate.

• Schnittstellenführung: Enger Austausch und Abstimmung mit Unternehmern, Behörden, Fachplanern sowie Vertretern aus Lehre und Forschung.

• Die Stelle ist vorerst auf maximal fünf Jahre befristet, zunächst mit einem Einjahresvertrag mit Verlängerungsoptionen.

Profil

Um die Anforderungen dieser anspruchsvollen Position ideal zu erfüllen, bringen Sie folgendes Profil mit:

• Ausbildung: Abgeschlossenes Studium in Architektur (ETH/FH oder gleichwertig).

• Berufserfahrung: Fundierte, mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Ausführungsplanung und Projektkoordination in der Schweiz. Nachweisbare Erfahrung über alle SIA-Phasen ist zwingend erforderlich.

• Fachkenntnisse: Hervorragende Kenntnisse der Schweizer Bauvorschriften, Normen (SIA) und Bewilligungsverfahren, idealerweise mit Erfahrung im Bauen im Bestand.

• CAD-Kenntnisse: Sehr gute, praxiserprobte Kenntnisse in 3D-CAD, vorzugsweise Rhino und VisualArq oder vergleichbaren BIM-Systemen.

• Persönlichkeit: Strukturierte, selbständige Arbeitsweise, ausgeprägtes Verantwortungsbewusstsein, Flexibilität und Freude an unkonventionellen, innovativen Baulösungen.

• Sprachen: Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sowie gute Englischkenntnisse.

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

• Abwechslungsreiche Projektbearbeitung an der Schnittstelle von Architektur, Forschung und Praxis.

• Ihr Arbeitsort ist im neuen Projektbüro im HIL-Gebäude auf dem ETH-Campus Hönggerberg.

• Ihre Position ist dem Projektteam im Departement Architektur angegliedert.

• Wir bieten attraktive Arbeitsbedingungen in einem dynamischen, innovativen und internationalen Umfeld.

• Sie arbeiten eigenverantwortlich und in ständigem kollegialem Austausch mit unserem Team und einer Vielfalt an Partner:innen und Anspruchsgruppen.

Responsabilità Dans ce rôle lié au projet, vous assumerez les tâches et responsabilités suivantes : - Gestion des sous-projets : Gestion auto-responsable, coordination et mise en oeuvre de sous-projets spécifiques (p. ex. réhabilitation en cours d'exploitation, augmentation innovante). - Phases 1 à 5 de l'EIS : Traitement et contrôle complets des projets pour toutes les phases de performance de l'EIS, de l'étude préliminaire à la mise en oeuvre et mise en service réussies. - Prototypage : planification détaillée et exécution de constructions hautement innovantes, circulaires et prototypiques en collaboration directe avec les professeurs participants. - Contrôle de projet : responsabilité stricte pour respecter les délais, les qualités et les coûts dans l'immobilier et les processus de la ETH. - Gestion de l'interface : Échange et coordination étroits avec les entrepreneurs, les autorités, les planificateurs spécialisés ainsi que les représentants de l'enseignement et de la recherche. - Le poste est limité à un maximum de cinq ans, avec un contrat d'un an avec des options de prolongation.

Une expérience éprouvée sur toutes les phases de l'EIS est obligatoire. - Connaissance professionnelle : Excellente connaissance des règlements, normes (SIA) et procédures d'approbation suisses, idéalement avec une expérience dans la construction dans le bâtiment existant. - Compétences en CAO : Très bonne connaissance, éprouvée et éprouvée de CAO 3D, de préférence des deux systèmes, c'est-à-dire des deux systèmes du BIM. - Personnalité : Méthodes de travail structurées, indépendantes, un fort sens des responsabilités, flexibilité et joie dans les solutions de construction non conventionnelles et innovantes. - Langues : Très bonne compétence allemande et bonne compétence en anglais. Per il team di progettazione del Living Lab HIL, siamo alla ricerca di una persona leader-esperti e profilati che assuma il controllo strategico e operativo di tutta la fase di pianificazione e supporti la gestione complessiva del progetto. In questa funzione chiave, si controllano i processi complessi con la barra generale e garantire che gli obiettivi del progetto siano raggiunti con successo. Descrizione del lavoro In questo ruolo legato al progetto assumerai i seguenti compiti e responsabilità:
• Gestione del progetto Pianificazione: Responsabilità complessiva per il controllo operativo, il monitoraggio e il coordinamento di tutte le fasi di pianificazione del progetto di costruzione Living Lab HIL.
• Comunicazione globale del fornitore: Gestione del piombo, gestione della negoziazione e scambio strutturato con il fornitore esterno generale e i pianificatori specializzati.
• Gestione delle interfacce: coordinamento centrale tra ETH Real Estate, il provider globale, il team di integrazione di insegnamento e ricerca e il team di pianificazione.
• Gestione della partecipazione: stretta collaborazione con la gestione, assunzione di compiti di gestione operativa e rappresentazione degli interessi dei progetti nei comitati strategici.
• Gestione del rischio e della qualità: garantire gli obiettivi generali del progetto in termini di scadenze, costi, obiettivi di sostenibilità e qualità nel complesso contesto della ricerca e della pratica costruttiva.
• La posizione è limitata ad un massimo di cinque anni, inizialmente con un contratto di un anno con opzioni di estensione. Profilo Per soddisfare i requisiti di questa posizione impegnativa idealmente, si dispone del seguente profilo:
• Formazione: Laurea magistrale in architettura (ETH/FH o comparabile).
• Esperienza professionale: Esperienza consolidata e consolidata nella gestione dei progetti e controllo globale di complessi progetti di costruzione su larga scala in Svizzera. L'esperienza con la costruzione nell'edificio esistente è vantaggiosa.
• esperienza GP: esperienza evidenziata nella gestione contrattuale ed operativa dei team di gestione generali e nell'impegnativo coordinamento interdisciplinare.
• Mente: Espresso pensiero strategico e imprenditoriale, abbinato ad una competenza di implementazione pragmatica e orientata agli obiettivi.
• Leadership: potenziale di leadership Recognizable o già comprovata esperienza in una funzione di gestione o gestione.
• Conoscenza CAD: Ottime conoscenze, collaudate in CAD 3D, preferibilmente in termini sia di prestazioni del sistema che del sistema BIM.
• Lingue: Ottima conoscenza tedesca e buona conoscenza inglese. Posizione Offriamo
• vario processo di progetto all'interfaccia di architettura, ricerca e pratica.
• La vostra posizione di lavoro è nel nuovo ufficio di progetto nel HIL edificio sul campus ETH Hönggerberg.
• La vostra posizione è allegata al team di progetto del Dipartimento di Architettura.
• Offriamo condizioni di lavoro attraenti in un ambiente dinamico, innovativo e internazionale.
• Lavorate in modo indipendente e in continuo scambio di informazioni con il nostro team e con una varietà di partner: interni ed esterni.

Architect:in / Project Manager:in planning (m/w/d) 100%, Zurich, limited print Print ETH Zurich is launching a pioneering research project with a direct connection to building practice with the "Living Lab HIL".The HIL building on the Hönggerberg Campus is becoming a real laboratory.The construction that needs to be rehabilitated is being rebuilt and expanded.In the coming years, professors from the Departments of Architecture (D-ARCH) as well as the Construction, Environment and Geomatics (D-BAUG) will be researching and planning the renovation of the HIL building in the sense of circular construction. The aim is to further develop sustainable design and construction in the existing building and to apply it in an exemplar way to a real planning and construction project. For the planning team of the Living Lab HIL, we are looking for a leader-experienced and profiled person who takes over the strategic and operational control of the entire planning phase and supports the overall project management. In this key function, you control the complex processes with the overall bar and ensure that the project goals are successfully achieved. Job Description In this project-related role you will take on the following tasks and responsibilities:
• Project management Planning: Overall responsibility for the operational control, monitoring and coordination of all planning phases of the construction project Living Lab HIL.
• Overall provider communication: Lead management, negotiation management and structured exchange with the external overall provider and the specialist planners.
• Interface management: Central coordination between ETH Real Estate, the overall provider, the team of teaching and research integration and the planning team.
• Participation Management: Close cooperation with the management, taking on operational management tasks and representing project interests in strategic committees.
• Risk and quality management: Ensuring the overall project goals in terms of deadlines, costs, sustainability targets and qualities in the complex context of research and construction practice.
• The position is limited to a maximum of five years, initially with a one-year contract with extension options. Profile To meet the requirements of this demanding position ideally, you have the following profile:
• Education: Master's degree in architecture (ETH/FH or comparable).
• Professional experience: Well-founded, long-standing experience in project management and overall control of complex large-scale construction projects in Switzerland. Experience with construction in the existing building is advantageous.
• GP experience: evidenced experience in the contractual and operational management of overall management teams as well as in the demanding, interdisciplinary coordination.
• Mindset: Expressed strategic and entrepreneurial thinking, coupled with a pragmatic, goal-oriented implementation competence.
• Leadership: Recognizable leadership potential or already proven experience in a managing or management function.
• CAD knowledge: Very good, tried-and-tested knowledge in 3D CAD, preferably in terms of both the performance of the system and the BIM system.
• Languages: Very good German knowledge and good English knowledge. Location We offer
• varied project processing at the interface of architecture, research and practice.
• Your work location is in the new project office in the HIL building on the ETH campus Hönggerberg.
• Your position is attached to the project team in the Department of Architecture.
• We offer attractive working conditions in a dynamic, innovative and international environment.
• You work independently and in constant collegial exchange with our team as well as a variety of partners: inside and out.

Drucken

The Macromolecular Engineering Laboratory (Prof. Mark W. Tibbitt) within the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering (D-MAVT) at ETH Zürich, Switzerland engineers and applies advanced polymeric materials and medical devices for a range of biomedical and industrial uses. The recent focus of the group includes the development of: (i) rational design of dynamic polymer networks; (ii) (bio)material processing; (iii) organ perfusion and regeneration; (iv) tools to study mechanobiology and cell–matrix interactions; and (v) engineered drug delivery systems. The lab is composed of a highly interdisciplinary and international team of motivated researchers. To expand on our expertise in machine perfusion device design and extend our platforms to new biological systems, we are recruiting a full-time (100%) doctoral candidate with a background in electrical or mechanical engineering, with an intended starting date on or after 01. September 2026.

Project background

The Macromolecular Engineering Laboratory has a long-standing research program in the engineering of ex situ organ perfusion systems, developed as part of the interdisciplinary Liver4Life project in collaboration with the University Hospital Zürich and the Wyss Zürich Translational Center. Over the past decade, the lab co-developed a normothermic machine perfusion platform that replicates key physiological functions — including pulsatile circulation, oxygenation, dialysis, and hormone and nutrient supplementation — to maintain organs viable outside the body for extended periods. This work culminated in world-first demonstrations of human liver preservation for one week ex situ [Eshmuminov et al. Nat. Biotechnol. 2020] and the first clinical transplantation of a liver treated and recovered in a perfusion machine [Clavien et al. Nat. Biotechnol. 2022]. In parallel, the lab has developed a compact machine perfusion platform for rat liver, enabling fundamental studies of organ metabolism, pharmacology, and perfusion biomarker discovery under controlled ex situ conditions.

Tibbitt) im Departement Maschinenbau und Verfahrenstechnik (D-MAVT) der ETH Zürich, Schweiz, entwickelt und wendet hochentwickelte Polymermaterialien und Medizinprodukte für eine Vielzahl biomedizinischer und industrieller Anwendungen an. Der jüngste Fokus der Gruppe umfasst die Entwicklung von: (i) rationalen Design von dynamischen Polymernetzwerken; (ii) (Bio)Materialverarbeitung; (iii) Organperfusion und Regeneration; (iv) Werkzeugen zur Erforschung der Mechanobiologie und Zell-Matrix-Interaktionen; und (v) entwickelter Arzneimittelliefersysteme. Das Labor besteht aus einem hochinterdisziplinären und internationalen Team motivierter Forscher. Um unsere Expertise im Maschinenperfusionsgerätedesign auszubauen und unsere Plattformen auf neue biologische Systeme auszudehnen, rekrutieren wir einen Vollzeit-Doktoranden (100%) mit einem Hintergrund in Elektro- oder Maschinenbau, mit einem geplanten Startdatum am oder nach dem 01. September 2026. Projekthintergrund Das Macromolecular Engineering Laboratory verfügt über ein langjähriges Forschungsprogramm zur Entwicklung von Ex-situ-Organperfusionssystemen, das im Rahmen des interdisziplinären Liver4Life-Projekts in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Universitätsklinikum Zürich und dem Wyss Zürich Translational Center entwickelt wurde. Im Laufe des letzten Jahrzehnts entwickelte das Labor eine normamemische Maschinenperfusionsplattform, die wichtige physiologische Funktionen repliziert – einschließlich pulsatile Zirkulation, Sauerstoffversorgung, Dialyse, Hormon- und Nährstoffsupplementierung – um Organe, die außerhalb des Körpers lebensfähig sind, über längere Zeiträume hinweg zu erhalten. Diese Arbeit gipfelte in weltweit ersten Demonstrationen der menschlichen Lebererhaltung für eine Woche ex situ [Eshmuminov et al. Nat. Biotechnol. 2020] und der ersten klinischen Transplantation einer Leber, die in einer Perfusionsmaschine behandelt und wiedergefunden wurde [Clavien et al. Nat. Biotechnol. 2022]. Parallel dazu hat das Labor eine kompakte Maschinenperfusionsplattform für Rattenleber entwickelt, die grundlegende Studien zum Organstoffwechsel, zur Pharmakologie und zur Entdeckung des Perfusionsbiomarkers unter kontrollierten Ex-situ-Bedingungen ermöglicht. jobs.description:
PhD student for High-ResolutionTime-Resolved Microstructural Evolution Under Ion Irradiation via TEM

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

ETH Zürich is one of the world’s leading universities, specializing in science and technology. It is renowned for its excellent education, its cutting-edge fundamental research and its efforts to put new knowledge and innovations directly into practice. The Laboratory of Metal Physics and Technology (LMPT), part of the Department of Materials at ETH Zürich, conducts research and teaching in areas ranging from basic science to technology, mostly in metal-related areas. It is led by Jörg F. Löffler and brings together physicists, materials scientists, chemists and biomedical engineers from across the world. It creates novel materials and explores emerging phenomena in metal physics and technology via detailed materials analysis and modeling.

The Ernst Ruska-Centre for Microscopy and Spectroscopy with Electrons (ER-C) at the Jülich Research Center (FZ Jülich) hosts one of the world’s most advanced transmission electron microscopy (TEM) facilities. It houses an unparalleled collection of state-of-the-art instruments, which enable ultrahigh-resolution studies of materials and devices with unparalleled spatial, energy and temporal resolution.

Project background

Are you ready to dive into Materials Science?

We are looking for a PhD candidate to work at ER-C (Forschungszentrum Jülich) and LMPT (ETH Zürich) to investigate high-resolution, real-time microstructural evolution in materials under ion irradiation and thus to understand in detail the performance of materials in e.g. future fusion reactors or particle accelerators and in general to understand materials driven far out from equilibrium. In situ TEM and Dynamic TEM (DTEM) are powerful techniques that can be used to reveal microstructure–property relationships in materials under operational conditions, which remains largely unexplored for ion-irradiated materials. Despite decades of research, the fundamental mechanisms governing the sub-nanosecond displacement cascade evolution, and the resulting defect dynamics and irradiation-induced phase transitions are incompletely understood, especially in the presence of realistic external stimuli.

Project Overview

The successful candidate will utilize advanced analytical and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM)—including collaborations at the ER-C—to directly observe structural changes at the atomic level. Fast scanning calorimetry and synchrotron radiation techniques will be employed to probe the kinetics and thermodynamics of phase transformations. The project will explore how temperature, mechanical strain, and irradiation induce changes in atomic structure and dynamics. The influence of atomic arrangement on stability, transformation kinetics, and crystallization will be systematically investigated.

Job description

• Studies of defect dynamics and phase transitions: In situ and Dynamic TEM using controlled ion irradiation

• Nanoscale microstructure analysis: Time-resolved TEM and complementary ex situ characterization

• Simulation and modelling: Molecular dynamics, kinetic Monte Carlo and kinetic rate theory

• Data analysis and interpretation: Drawing conclusions from experimental and simulated data

• Scientific reporting: Publishing and presenting research findings

• Collaborative research: Contributions to group projects at ETH Zürich and FZ Jülich

• Teaching: Contributions to practicals and lecture assignments at ETH Zürich and FZ Jülich

Profile

A Master’s degree in physics, materials science, or a related discipline, including:

• Background in solid-state physics and a demonstrated interest in experimental research

• Familiarity with scientific programming or atomistic simulations

• Proficiency in oral and written English

Studente di dottorato per alta risoluzione Evoluzione microstrutturale risolta a tempo nell'Irradiazione Ionica tramite TEM 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo ETH Zürich è una delle principali università del mondo, specializzata nella scienza e nella tecnologia. È rinomata per la sua eccellente educazione, la sua ricerca fondamentale all'avanguardia e i suoi sforzi per mettere in pratica nuove conoscenze e innovazioni. Il Laboratorio di Fisica e Tecnologia dei Metalli (LMPT), parte del Dipartimento dei Materiali di ETH Zürich, conduce la ricerca e l'insegnamento in aree che vanno dalla scienza di base alla tecnologia, per lo più in settori legati al metallo. È guidato da Jörg F. Löffler e riunisce fisici, scienziati dei materiali, chimici e ingegneri biomedici di tutto il mondo. Crea nuovi materiali ed esplora i fenomeni emergenti nella fisica e nella tecnologia dei metalli attraverso l'analisi dettagliata dei materiali e la modellazione. Ernst Ruska-Centre per la microscopia e la spettroscopia con elettroni (ER-C) presso il Centro di Ricerca Jülich (FZ Jülich) ospita uno dei più avanzati impianti di microscopia elettronica di trasmissione (TEM). Ospita una collezione senza pari di strumenti all'avanguardia, che consentono studi a ultraalta risoluzione di materiali e dispositivi con una risoluzione spaziale, energetica e temporale senza pari. Sfondo del progetto Sei pronto a immergerti nella Scienza dei Materiali? Stiamo cercando un Dottorato di Ricerca per lavorare presso ER-C (Forschungszentrum Jülich) e LMPT (ETH Zürich) per indagare l'evoluzione microstrutturale ad alta risoluzione in tempo reale nei materiali sotto irradiazione ionica e quindi per capire in dettaglio le prestazioni dei materiali in reattori di fusione futuri o acceleratori di particelle e in generale per capire i materiali lontani dall'equilibrio. In situ TEM e Dynamic TEM (DTEM) sono potenti tecniche che possono essere utilizzate per rivelare le relazioni microstruttura-property nei materiali in condizioni operative, che rimangono in gran parte inesplorate per i materiali ion-irradiated. Nonostante decenni di ricerca, i meccanismi fondamentali che regolano l'evoluzione della cascata di spostamento del sub-nanosecondo e le dinamiche difetti e le transizioni di fase indotte dall'irradiazione sono incompleti, soprattutto in presenza di stimoli esterni realistici. Panoramica del progetto Il candidato di successo utilizzerà la microscopia elettronica di trasmissione analitica e ad alta risoluzione (TEM) avanzata, comprese le collaborazioni al ER-C, per osservare direttamente i cambiamenti strutturali a livello atomico. La calorimetria di scansione rapida e le tecniche di radiazione sincrotronica saranno impiegate per sondare la cinetica e la termodinamica delle trasformazioni di fase. Il progetto esaminerà come la temperatura, la tensione meccanica e l'irradiazione inducono cambiamenti nella struttura e nella dinamica atomica. L'influenza della disposizione atomica sulla stabilità, la trasformazione cinetica e la cristallizzazione saranno sistematicamente indagati. Descrizione del lavoro
• Studi di dinamiche di difetto e transizioni di fase: In situ e Dynamic TEM mediante irraggiamento controllato
• Analisi della microstruttura nanoscala: TEM risolto nel tempo e caratterizzazione complementare ex situ
• Simulazione e modellazione: Dinamica molecolare, Monte Carlo cinetica e teoria dei tassi cinetici
• Analisi e interpretazione dei dati: trarre conclusioni dai dati sperimentali e simulati

ETH Zürich is one of the world’s leading universities, specializing in science and technology. It is renowned for its excellent education, its cutting-edge fundamental research and its efforts to put new knowledge and innovations directly into practice. The Laboratory of Metal Physics and Technology (LMPT), part of the Department of Materials at ETH Zürich, conducts research and teaching in areas ranging from basic science to technology, mostly in metal-related areas. It is led by Jörg F. Löffler and brings together physicists, materials scientists, chemists and biomedical engineers from across the world. It creates novel materials and explores emerging phenomena in metal physics and technology via detailed materials analysis and modeling.

The Ernst Ruska-Centre for Microscopy and Spectroscopy with Electrons (ER-C) at the Jülich Research Center (FZ Jülich) hosts one of the world’s most advanced transmission electron microscopy (TEM) facilities. It houses an unparalleled collection of state-of-the-art instruments, which enable ultrahigh-resolution studies of materials and devices with unparalleled spatial, energy and temporal resolution.

Project background

Are you ready to dive into Materials Science?

We are looking for a PhD candidate to work at ER-C (Forschungszentrum Jülich) and LMPT (ETH Zürich) to investigate high-resolution, real-time microstructural evolution in materials under ion irradiation and thus to understand in detail the performance of materials in e.g. future fusion reactors or particle accelerators and in general to understand materials driven far out from equilibrium. In situ TEM and Dynamic TEM (DTEM) are powerful techniques that can be used to reveal microstructure–property relationships in materials under operational conditions, which remains largely unexplored for ion-irradiated materials. Despite decades of research, the fundamental mechanisms governing the sub-nanosecond displacement cascade evolution, and the resulting defect dynamics and irradiation-induced phase transitions are incompletely understood, especially in the presence of realistic external stimuli.

Project Overview

The successful candidate will utilize advanced analytical and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM)—including collaborations at the ER-C—to directly observe structural changes at the atomic level. Fast scanning calorimetry and synchrotron radiation techniques will be employed to probe the kinetics and thermodynamics of phase transformations. The project will explore how temperature, mechanical strain, and irradiation induce changes in atomic structure and dynamics. The influence of atomic arrangement on stability, transformation kinetics, and crystallization will be systematically investigated.

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering (LESE, ETH Zürich) invites applications for a PhD position in the field of CO₂ capture and critical element recovery, with a focus on atomic-scale structure–performance relationships in separation materials. This PhD position is funded by the National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) Separations , and is carried out under the co-supervision of Dr. Paula Abdala and Prof. Christoph R. Müller.

Project background

The aim of this project is to establish a fundamental understanding of how atomic structure governs selectivity, capacity, and stability in materials for CO₂ capture and for the recovery of valuable elements such as lithium and cobalt from complex waste streams. These applications are key to enabling sustainable carbon management and circular resource use.

Job description

• The research combines the synthesis of model materials with advanced structural and spectroscopic characterization, with a strong emphasis on X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray total scattering with pair distribution function analysis, and vibrational spectroscopy

• These techniques will be used to probe local coordination environments, electronic structure, and structural dynamics under working conditions.

• The project is embedded in a highly interdisciplinary environment, linking experimental materials chemistry with computational screening and process modelling

• The overarching goal is to connect atomic-scale mechanisms directly to their separation performance and to derive rational design principles for improved materials

Profile

• Excellent MSc degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemistry, or related field

• Experience in materials synthesis and characterization is an advantage

• Strong motivation, creativity, and ability to work independently and in teams

• Interest in atomic-scale mechanisms in separation materials

• High degree of independence and self-organization

• Willingness to work in an interdisciplinary and evolving research project

• Flexibility for intensive experimental campaigns, including synchrotron beamtime

PhD opening in material science of stone conservation

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair for Physical Chemistry of Building Materials has one opening for PhD. position on the topic of stone conservation, in particular the mechanisms of contour scaling. This PhD is part of the collaborative project “Spatially graded 3D printing to elucidate contour scaling of building stones”. It aims at elucidating the mechanism of contour scaling on building stone, establishing on-site monitoring methods and testing possible treatments for it. The selected student will collaborate with another PhD candidate funded in the scheme and employed at the Chair for Digital Building Technologies in the Department of Architecture.

Project background

This project aims to establish and validate a novel experimental approach to the study of stone deterioration by leveraging powder-bed 3D printing of stone-like materials. This enables the creation of spatially graded samples mimicking natural stones and their alteration through weathering. Most importantly, this can be done in a repetitive way and with systematic variations of the defect, flaws and inhomogeneities known to play an essential role in stone deterioration.

The specific stone deterioration mechanism that will be investigated is contour scaling, a process of particular concern to molasse sandstones largely used in the Swiss plateau. It leads to loss of cohesion below the exposed surface, at a depth in the range of some millimetres to several centimetres. It leads to highly inhomogeneous properties that our 3D printing approach would be able to mimic for the first time.

The 3D printing will begin using an innovative and large-scale 3D powder bed printer developed by the Chair for Digital Building Technologies, and will be advanced for the purpose of this project by the other PhD student.

Job description

• The present PhD student will use such 3D printed stones in the unique testing facilities of the Chair for Physical Chemistry of Building Materials

• This will enable the reproduction under laboratory conditions of harsh events that condition the weathering of building stones on monuments

• That study will be complemented by method development to enable rapid detection of contour scales on site, in addition to exploring possible means of halting the propagation and/or formation of such contour scales

Profile

• The successful candidate should have a keen interest, or preferably experience in heritage conservation science

• They should additionally hold a Masters degree in conservation science, material science, chemistry, chemical engineering, civil engineering, or conservation architecture

• In any case good experimental skills are a must

• An excellent oral and written level of English is essential

• Conversational knowledge of German is an advantage, but desire to learn it is a must

• As the project involves collaboration between groups in addition to field practitioners, very good communication skills and willingness to collaborate with other researchers is essential

Workplace

We offer

The Chair of Physical Chemistry of Building Materials within the Institute for Building Materials offers many chances for jump-starting an academic or industrial research career in cement and concrete technology, with a strong basis in materials chemistry and rheology. Our highly diverse and international group also offers many networking opportunities through academic societies such as RILEM, industry connections, as well as internal ETH connections. Apertura del dottorato in scienze materiali di conservazione della pietra 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La sedia per Chimica Fisica dei Materiali Edili ha un'apertura per la posizione di dottorato sul tema della conservazione della pietra, in particolare i meccanismi di contorno scaling. Questo dottorato fa parte del progetto collaborativo “Spatially graded 3D Print to elucidate contorno scaling di pietre da costruzione”. Esso mira a elucidare il meccanismo di contorno scaling su pietra da costruzione, stabilendo metodi di monitoraggio in loco e testando possibili trattamenti per esso. Lo studente selezionato collaborerà con un altro candidato di dottorato finanziato nel progetto e impiegato presso la Cattedra per le tecnologie di costruzione digitale nel Dipartimento di Architettura. Sfondo del progetto Questo progetto mira a stabilire e convalidare un nuovo approccio sperimentale allo studio del deterioramento della pietra sfruttando la stampa 3D in polvere di materiali simili a pietre. Ciò consente la creazione di campioni di livello spaziale che imitano le pietre naturali e la loro alterazione attraverso le intemperie. Soprattutto, questo può essere fatto in modo ripetitivo e con variazioni sistematiche del difetto, dei difetti e delle omogeneità note per svolgere un ruolo essenziale nel deterioramento della pietra. Lo specifico meccanismo di deterioramento della pietra che verrà indagato è il contorno di scaling, un processo di particolare preoccupazione per la molasse arenaria in gran parte utilizzata nell'altopiano svizzero. Essa porta alla perdita di coesione sotto la superficie esposta, a una profondità nella gamma di alcuni millimetri a diversi centimetri. Porta a proprietà altamente inomogenee che il nostro approccio di stampa 3D sarebbe in grado di imitare per la prima volta. La stampa 3D inizierà ad utilizzare una stampante 3D innovativa e su larga scala sviluppata dalla Chair for Digital Building Technologies, e sarà avanzata allo scopo di questo progetto dall'altro dottorando. Descrizione del lavoro
• L'attuale studente di dottorato utilizzerà tali pietre stampate 3D negli impianti di prova unici della sedia per chimica fisica dei materiali da costruzione
• Ciò consentirà la riproduzione in condizioni di laboratorio di eventi difficili che condizionano il tempo di costruire pietre su monumenti
• Tale studio sarà completato dallo sviluppo dei metodi per consentire un rapido rilevamento delle scale di contorno in loco, oltre ad esplorare possibili mezzi di fermare la propagazione e/o la formazione di tali scale di contorno Profilo
• Il candidato di successo dovrebbe avere un interesse acuto, o preferibilmente esperienza nella scienza della conservazione del patrimonio
• Essi dovrebbero inoltre tenere un master in scienze della conservazione, scienza materiale, chimica, ingegneria chimica, ingegneria civile, o architettura di conservazione
• In ogni caso le buone capacità sperimentali sono un must
• Un eccellente livello orale e scritto di inglese è essenziale
• La conoscenza conversazionale del tedesco è un vantaggio, ma il desiderio di imparare è un must
• Poiché il progetto prevede la collaborazione tra gruppi oltre ai professionisti del settore, è essenziale saper comunicare molto bene e la disponibilità a collaborare con altri ricercatori. Luogo di lavoro Offriamo La Cattedra di Chimica Fisica dei Materiali Edili all'interno dell'Istituto per i Materiali Edili offre molte possibilità per avviare una carriera di ricerca accademica o industriale nella tecnologia del cemento e del cemento, con una forte base nella chimica dei materiali e nella reologia. Il nostro gruppo altamente diversificato e internazionale offre anche molte opportunità di networking attraverso società accademiche come RILEM, connessioni del settore, così come connessioni ETH interne. PhD Eröffnung in der Materialwissenschaft der Steinkonservierung 100%, Zürich, befristet Druck Druckerzeugnisse Der Lehrstuhl für Physikalische Chemie von Baustoffen hat eine Position zum Thema Steinschutz, insbesondere zu den Mechanismen der Konturskalierung. Diese Promotion ist Teil des Verbundprojekts „Räumlich abgestufter 3D-Druck zur Aufklärung der Konturskalierung von Bausteinen. Es zielt darauf ab, den Mechanismus der Konturskalierung auf dem Baustein aufzuklären, Überwachungsmethoden vor Ort zu etablieren und mögliche Behandlungen dafür zu testen. Der ausgewählte Student wird mit einem anderen Doktoranden zusammenarbeiten, der im Rahmen des Programms finanziert und am Lehrstuhl für digitale Gebäudetechnologien in der Architekturabteilung beschäftigt ist. Projekthintergrund Dieses Projekt zielt darauf ab, einen neuartigen experimentellen Ansatz zur Untersuchung des Steinverfalls durch den Einsatz des Pulverbett-3D-Drucks von steinähnlichen Materialien zu etablieren und zu validieren. Dies ermöglicht die Erstellung von räumlich abgestuften Proben, die Natursteine nachahmen und deren Veränderung durch Verwitterung. Am wichtigsten ist, dass dies auf wiederholte Weise und mit systematischen Variationen des Defekts, der Fehler und Inhomogenitäten erfolgen kann, von denen bekannt ist, dass sie eine wesentliche Rolle bei der Steinverschlechterung spielen. Der spezifische Steinverschlechterungsmechanismus, der untersucht wird, ist die Konturskalierung, ein Prozess, der für Melassesandsteine, die hauptsächlich auf dem Schweizer Plateau verwendet werden, von besonderer Bedeutung ist. Es führt zu einem Kohäsionsverlust unterhalb der exponierten Oberfläche in einer Tiefe im Bereich von einigen Millimetern bis zu mehreren Zentimetern. Es führt zu sehr inhomogenen Eigenschaften, die unser 3D-Druck-Ansatz zum ersten Mal nachahmen könnte. Der 3D-Druck wird mit einem innovativen und großformatigen 3D-Pulverbettdrucker beginnen, der vom Lehrstuhl für digitale Gebäudetechnologien entwickelt wurde, und wird für den Zweck dieses Projekts von dem anderen Doktoranden weiterentwickelt. Stellenbeschreibung
• Der jetzige Doktorand wird solche 3D-gedruckten Steine in den einzigartigen Testeinrichtungen des Lehrstuhls für Physikalische Chemie von Baustoffen verwenden.
• Dies ermöglicht die Reproduktion von harten Ereignissen unter Laborbedingungen, die die Verwitterung von Bausteinen auf Denkmälern beeinflussen.
• Diese Studie wird durch die Entwicklung von Methoden ergänzt, die eine schnelle Erkennung von Konturskalen vor Ort ermöglichen, zusätzlich zur Untersuchung möglicher Mittel zur Verhinderung der Ausbreitung und/oder Bildung solcher Konturskalen. Profil
• Der erfolgreiche Kandidat sollte ein großes Interesse oder vorzugsweise Erfahrung in der Wissenschaft zur Erhaltung des kulturellen Erbes haben.
• Sie sollten zusätzlich einen Master-Abschluss in Konservierungswissenschaften, Materialwissenschaften, Chemie, Chemietechnik, Bauingenieurwesen oder Konservierungsarchitektur haben
• Gute experimentelle Fähigkeiten sind in jedem Fall ein Muss
• Ein ausgezeichnetes mündliches und schriftliches Englischniveau ist unerlässlich
• Konversationskenntnisse in Deutsch sind ein Vorteil, aber der Wunsch, es zu lernen, ist ein Muss
• Da das Projekt die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Gruppen neben Praktikern vor Ort beinhaltet, sind sehr gute Kommunikationsfähigkeiten und die Bereitschaft zur Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Forschern unerlässlich. Ouverture du doctorat en science matérielle de la conservation de la pierre 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée La chaire de chimie physique des matériaux de construction a une ouverture pour le doctorat. position sur le thème de la conservation de la pierre, en particulier les mécanismes de l'échelle de contour. Ce doctorat s'inscrit dans le cadre du projet de collaboration. Il vise à élucider le mécanisme d'échelle des contours sur la pierre de construction, à établir des méthodes de surveillance sur place et à tester les traitements possibles. L'étudiant sélectionné collaborera avec un autre candidat au doctorat financé dans le cadre du programme et sera employé à la Chaire des technologies de construction numérique du Département d'architecture. Contexte du projet Ce projet vise à établir et à valider une nouvelle approche expérimentale de l'étude de la détérioration de la pierre en tirant parti de l'impression 3D par lit de poudre de matériaux de type pierre. Cela permet la création d'échantillons classés dans l'espace mimichant les pierres naturelles et leur altération par l'altération. Plus important encore, cela peut être fait de façon répétitive et avec des variations systématiques des défauts, défauts et inhomogénéités connus pour jouer un rôle essentiel dans la détérioration de la pierre. Le mécanisme spécifique de détérioration de la pierre qui sera étudié est l'échelle de contour, un processus particulièrement préoccupant pour les grès molasques largement utilisés sur le plateau suisse. Il entraîne une perte de cohésion sous la surface exposée, à une profondeur de quelques millimètres à plusieurs centimètres. Il conduit à des propriétés hautement inhomogènes que notre approche d'impression 3D serait en mesure d'imiter pour la première fois. L'impression 3D commencera à utiliser une imprimante 3D 3D innovante et à grande échelle développée par la Chaire des technologies de construction numérique, et sera avancée aux fins de ce projet par l'autre doctorant. Description de l'emploi
• Le doctorant actuel utilisera ces pierres imprimées 3D dans les installations d'essai uniques de la Chaire de chimie physique des matériaux de construction
• Cela permettra la reproduction dans des conditions de laboratoire d'événements difficiles qui conditionnent l'altération des pierres de construction sur les monuments
• Cette étude sera complétée par l'élaboration de méthodes permettant la détection rapide des échelles de contour sur place, en plus d'explorer les moyens possibles d'arrêter la propagation et/ou la formation de telles échelles de contour Profil
• Le candidat retenu devrait avoir un vif intérêt, ou de préférence une expérience en sciences de la conservation du patrimoine
• Ils devraient également détenir une maîtrise en sciences de la conservation, sciences des matériaux, chimie, génie chimique, génie civil ou architecture de conservation
• En tout état de cause, de bonnes compétences expérimentales sont indispensables.
• Un excellent niveau d'anglais oral et écrit est essentiel
• La connaissance conversationnelle de l'allemand est un avantage, mais le désir d'apprendre est un must
• Comme le projet implique la collaboration entre les groupes en plus des praticiens de terrain, de très bonnes compétences en communication et la volonté de collaborer avec d'autres chercheurs sont essentielles. Lieu de travail Nous offrons La chaire de chimie physique des matériaux de construction de l'Institut des matériaux de construction offre de nombreuses chances de démarrer une carrière universitaire ou industrielle en recherche sur le ciment et la technologie du béton, avec une base solide en chimie des matériaux et en rhéologie. Notre groupe très diversifié et international offre également de nombreuses possibilités de réseautage à travers des sociétés académiques telles que RILEM, des connexions industrielles, ainsi que des connexions internes ETH. jobs.description:
PhD position for developing multi-physics models of planar inductors and transformers

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Laboratory for High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) at the Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering of ETH Zurich conducts internationally leading research on power electronic converter systems, which are required, for example, in future energy distribution systems for the integration of renewable energy sources or in traction applications/electric vehicles. Another research focus is on solid-state pulse modulators for medical applications (computer tomography/cancer treatment) and accelerators (CERN). For the design and optimisation of the various power electronic systems, we develop advanced multi-physics models/digital twins/virtual prototypes at the component as well as at the system level. For a new research project on planar magnetics for highly compact, low profile power electronic systems, we are looking for a: PhD candidate (100%) for developing multi-physics models of planar inductors and transformers

Job description

We are looking for highly motivated individuals with an outstanding academic background who are interested in pursuing a PhD in the important and multidisciplinary research area of modelling and optimising planar magnetic devices (inductors and transformers). Compact and highly efficient planar magnetic devices utilising for example PCB based winding structures are key components of many power electronic converters with a low profile, which are required for example for DC-DC converters (PoL-converters) in future data centres or in automotive applications for interconnecting the main drive battery with the 12V auxiliary battery. Planar magnetic devices are also often required in wireless charging/energy transfer systems, where they must be highly compact and efficient.

To push the efficiency and power density limits of such planar magnetic devices, you will develop multi-physics models of planar magnetics. These models will comprehensively describe the (HF) losses in the windings, the parasitic capacitances of the windings, and also the temperature distribution in the winding and also the core. Furthermore, you will develop models for designing the electrical insulation of the winding. Based on these models, you will work on optimising the core and winding geometry, as well as developing advanced cooling concepts for the windings and core. Based on the models and developed concepts, you will then identify technological barriers to power density of planar magnetics.

The developed models should be integrated into optimisation procedures for power electronic converter systems in a computationally efficient manner. This is essential for achieving outstanding system efficiencies and power densities, as well as gaining a competitive edge. The models are also part of an ongoing, wider modelling framework development project at HPE, offering the opportunity to collaborate with other PhD candidates on various modelling aspects.

For verifying the new cooling and winding concepts as well as the developed models, you will design and build different prototypes, including PE converter systems, to operate the planar magnetics under realistic conditions.

Our laboratory is offering a challenging and scientifically exciting full-time position within a dynamic international team at one of the world's leading technical universities. We also strongly encourage participation in international conferences and offer a competitive salary, excellent benefits, and outstanding research and laboratory facilities for your experiments.

Profile

• You must have a diploma/M.Sc. degree in electrical engineering with excellent grades

• Fundamental knowledge of power electronic converter systems

• Good communication skills

• Fluency in English

• The willingness to fully commit yourself as part of an international team.

Posizione di dottorato per lo sviluppo di modelli multi-fisici di induttori planari e trasformatori 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Laboratorio per sistemi elettronici ad alta potenza (HPE) presso il Dipartimento di Tecnologia dell'Informazione e Ingegneria Elettrica dell'ETH di Zurigo conduce ricerche leader a livello internazionale sui sistemi di conversione elettronica di potenza, che sono necessari, ad esempio, nei futuri sistemi di distribuzione dell'energia per l'integrazione di fonti di energia rinnovabile o nelle applicazioni di trazione / veicoli elettrici. Un'altra ricerca si concentra sui modulatori a impulsi a stato solido per applicazioni mediche (trattamento tomografia computer/cancro) e sugli acceleratori (CERN). Per la progettazione e l'ottimizzazione dei vari sistemi elettronici di potenza, sviluppiamo modelli multi-fisici avanzati / gemelli digitali / prototipi virtuali al componente e a livello di sistema. Per un nuovo progetto di ricerca sui magnetici planari per sistemi elettronici di potenza altamente compatti e di basso profilo, stiamo cercando un: Dottorato di ricerca (100%) per lo sviluppo di modelli multi-fisici di induttori planari e trasformatori Descrizione del lavoro Siamo alla ricerca di individui altamente motivati con un eccezionale background accademico che sono interessati a perseguire un dottorato nell'importante e multidisciplinare area di ricerca di modellazione e ottimizzazione dei dispositivi magnetici planari (induttori e trasformatori). I dispositivi magnetici planari compatti e altamente efficienti che utilizzano per esempio le strutture di avvolgimento basate su PCB sono componenti chiave di molti convertitori elettronici di potenza con un profilo basso, che sono necessari per esempio per i convertitori DC-DC (PoL-converter) nei centri di dati futuri o nelle applicazioni automobilistiche per collegare la batteria di azionamento principale con la batteria ausiliaria 12V. I dispositivi magnetici planari sono spesso richiesti anche nei sistemi di ricarica/di trasferimento di energia wireless, dove devono essere altamente compatti ed efficienti. Per spingere i limiti di efficienza e densità di potenza di tali dispositivi magnetici planari, svilupperai modelli multi-fisici di magnetici planari. Questi modelli descriveranno in modo completo le perdite (HF) negli avvolgimento, le capacità parassitarie degli avvolgimento, e anche la distribuzione della temperatura nell'avvolgimento e anche il nucleo. Inoltre, svilupperai modelli per la progettazione dell'isolamento elettrico dell'avvolgimento. Sulla base di questi modelli, si lavorerà sull'ottimizzazione della geometria del nucleo e dell'avvolgimento, oltre a sviluppare concetti di raffreddamento avanzati per gli avvolgimento e il nucleo. Sulla base dei modelli e dei concetti sviluppati, si identificano le barriere tecnologiche alla densità di potenza dei magnetici planari. I modelli sviluppati dovrebbero essere integrati in procedure di ottimizzazione per i sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza in modo computazionalmente efficiente. Questo è essenziale per raggiungere le efficienze del sistema e le densità di potenza eccezionali, così come ottenere un vantaggio competitivo. I modelli fanno parte anche di un continuo e più ampio progetto di sviluppo framework di modellazione presso HPE, offrendo l'opportunità di collaborare con altri candidati PhD su vari aspetti di modellazione. Per verificare i nuovi concetti di raffreddamento e avvolgimento così come i modelli sviluppati, si progetta e costruisce diversi prototipi, compresi i sistemi di convertitore PE, per operare i magnetici planari in condizioni realistiche. Il nostro laboratorio offre una posizione a tempo pieno impegnativo e scientificamente emozionante all'interno di un team internazionale dinamico in una delle principali università tecniche del mondo. Inoltre incoraggiamo fortemente la partecipazione a conferenze internazionali e offriamo uno stipendio competitivo, eccellenti vantaggi, e eccellenti strutture di ricerca e laboratorio per i vostri esperimenti. descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD position for developing multi-physics models of planar inductors and transformers

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Laboratory for High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) at the Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering of ETH Zurich conducts internationally leading research on power electronic converter systems, which are required, for example, in future energy distribution systems for the integration of renewable energy sources or in traction applications/electric vehicles. Another research focus is on solid-state pulse modulators for medical applications (computer tomography/cancer treatment) and accelerators (CERN). For the design and optimisation of the various power electronic systems, we develop advanced multi-physics models/digital twins/virtual prototypes at the component as well as at the system level. For a new research project on planar magnetics for highly compact, low profile power electronic systems, we are looking for a: PhD candidate (100%) for developing multi-physics models of planar inductors and transformers

Job description

We are looking for highly motivated individuals with an outstanding academic background who are interested in pursuing a PhD in the important and multidisciplinary research area of modelling and optimising planar magnetic devices (inductors and transformers). Compact and highly efficient planar magnetic devices utilising for example PCB based winding structures are key components of many power electronic converters with a low profile, which are required for example for DC-DC converters (PoL-converters) in future data centres or in automotive applications for interconnecting the main drive battery with the 12V auxiliary battery. Planar magnetic devices are also often required in wireless charging/energy transfer systems, where they must be highly compact and efficient.

To push the efficiency and power density limits of such planar magnetic devices, you will develop multi-physics models of planar magnetics. These models will comprehensively describe the (HF) losses in the windings, the parasitic capacitances of the windings, and also the temperature distribution in the winding and also the core. Furthermore, you will develop models for designing the electrical insulation of the winding. Based on these models, you will work on optimising the core and winding geometry, as well as developing advanced cooling concepts for the windings and core. Based on the models and developed concepts, you will then identify technological barriers to power density of planar magnetics.

The developed models should be integrated into optimisation procedures for power electronic converter systems in a computationally efficient manner. This is essential for achieving outstanding system efficiencies and power densities, as well as gaining a competitive edge. The models are also part of an ongoing, wider modelling framework development project at HPE, offering the opportunity to collaborate with other PhD candidates on various modelling aspects.

For verifying the new cooling and winding concepts as well as the developed models, you will design and build different prototypes, including PE converter systems, to operate the planar magnetics under realistic conditions.

Our laboratory is offering a challenging and scientifically exciting full-time position within a dynamic international team at one of the world's leading technical universities. We also strongly encourage participation in international conferences and offer a competitive salary, excellent benefits, and outstanding research and laboratory facilities for your experiments.

Profile

• You must have a diploma/M.Sc. degree in electrical engineering with excellent grades

• Fundamental knowledge of power electronic converter systems

• Good communication skills

• Fluency in English

• The willingness to fully commit yourself as part of an international team.

• In addition, you should be interested in the detailed mode

PhD Position für die Entwicklung von Multi-Physik-Modelle von planaren Induktoren und Transformatoren 100%, Zürich, befristet Druck Druckerzeugnisse Das Labor für Hochleistungselektronik (HPE) am Fachbereich Informationstechnik und Elektrotechnik der ETH Zürich betreibt international führende Forschung zu leistungselektronischen Wandlersystemen, die beispielsweise in zukünftigen Energieverteilungssystemen zur Integration erneuerbarer Energiequellen oder in Traktionsanwendungen/Elektrofahrzeugen benötigt werden. Ein weiterer Forschungsschwerpunkt liegt auf Festkörperpulsmodulatoren für medizinische Anwendungen (Computertomographie/Krebsbehandlung) und Beschleunigern (CERN). Für die Gestaltung und Optimierung der verschiedenen leistungselektronischen Systeme entwickeln wir fortschrittliche Multiphysikmodelle/digitale Zwillinge/virtuelle Prototypen auf Komponenten- und Systemebene. Für ein neues Forschungsprojekt zu Planarmagnetik für hochkompakt, Low Profile Leistungselektronik, suchen wir einen Doktoranden (100%) für die Entwicklung von Multi-Physik-Modellen von planaren Induktoren und Transformatoren. Stellenbeschreibung Wir suchen hochmotivierte Personen mit einem hervorragenden akademischen Hintergrund, die sich für eine Promotion im wichtigen und multidisziplinären Forschungsbereich der Modellierung und Optimierung planarer magnetischer Bauelemente (Induktoren und Transformatoren) interessieren. Kompakte und hocheffiziente planarmagnetische Bauelemente, die beispielsweise PCB-basierte Wicklungsstrukturen nutzen, sind Schlüsselkomponenten vieler leistungselektronischer Umrichter mit niedrigem Profil, die beispielsweise für DC-DC-Wandler (PoL-Wandler) in zukünftigen Rechenzentren oder in Automobilanwendungen zur Verschaltung der Hauptantriebsbatterie mit der 12V-Hilfsbatterie benötigt werden. Planare magnetische Geräte werden auch häufig in drahtlosen Lade-/Energieübertragungssystemen benötigt, wo sie sehr kompakt und effizient sein müssen. Um die Effizienz- und Leistungsdichtegrenzen solcher planaren magnetischen Geräte zu erweitern, werden Sie multiphysikalische Modelle der planaren Magnetik entwickeln. Diese Modelle werden die (HF-) Verluste in den Wicklungen, die parasitären Kapazitäten der Wicklungen sowie die Temperaturverteilung in der Wicklung und auch im Kern umfassend beschreiben. Darüber hinaus werden Sie Modelle für die Gestaltung der elektrischen Isolierung der Wicklung entwickeln. Basierend auf diesen Modellen arbeiten Sie an der Optimierung der Kern- und Wicklungsgeometrie sowie an der Entwicklung fortschrittlicher Kühlkonzepte für Wicklungen und Kern. Basierend auf den Modellen und entwickelten Konzepten werden Sie dann technologische Barrieren für die Leistungsdichte von planaren Magneten identifizieren. Die entwickelten Modelle sollten recheneffizient in Optimierungsverfahren für leistungselektronische Umrichtersysteme integriert werden. Dies ist unerlässlich, um hervorragende Systemeffizienzen und Leistungsdichten zu erzielen sowie einen Wettbewerbsvorteil zu erzielen. Die Modelle sind auch Teil eines laufenden, umfassenderen Modellierungsrahmenentwicklungsprojekts am HPE, das die Möglichkeit bietet, mit anderen Doktoranden an verschiedenen Modellierungsaspekten zusammenzuarbeiten. Um die neuen Kühl- und Wicklungskonzepte sowie die entwickelten Modelle zu verifizieren, entwerfen und bauen Sie verschiedene Prototypen, einschließlich PE-Konvertersystemen, um die Planarmagnete unter realistischen Bedingungen zu betreiben. Unser Labor bietet eine anspruchsvolle und wissenschaftlich spannende Vollzeitstelle in einem dynamischen internationalen Team an einer der weltweit führenden technischen Universitäten. Wir empfehlen auch die Teilnahme an internationalen Konferenzen und bieten ein wettbewerbsfähiges Gehalt, hervorragende Vorteile und hervorragende Forschungs- und Laboreinrichtungen für Ihre Experimente. Profil
• Sie müssen ein Diplom / M.Sc. in Elektrotechnik mit ausgezeichneten Noten haben
• Grundlegende Kenntnisse der Leistungselektronik
• Gute Kommunikationsfähigkeit
• Fluency in Englisch
• Die Bereitschaft, sich als Teil eines internationalen Teams voll und ganz zu engagieren.
• Darüber hinaus sollten Sie sich für den detaillierten Modus interessieren

Poste de doctorat pour le développement de modèles multiphysiques d'inducteurs et de transformateurs planaires 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée Le Laboratoire des systèmes électroniques de haute puissance (HPE) du Département des technologies de l'information et de l'ingénierie électrique de l'ETH de Zurich effectue des recherches de pointe sur les systèmes de convertisseurs électroniques de puissance, qui sont nécessaires, par exemple, dans les futurs systèmes de distribution d'énergie pour l'intégration des sources d'énergie renouvelables ou dans les applications de traction/véhicules électriques. La recherche porte également sur les modulateurs d'impulsions à l'état solide pour les applications médicales (tomographie par ordinateur/traitement du cancer) et les accélérateurs (CERN). Pour la conception et l'optimisation des différents systèmes électroniques de puissance, nous développons des modèles multiphysiques avancés, des jumeaux numériques et des prototypes virtuels au niveau du composant ainsi qu'au niveau du système. Pour un nouveau projet de recherche sur les magnétiques planaires pour les systèmes électroniques à faible puissance très compacts, nous recherchons un candidat au doctorat (100 %) pour développer des modèles multiphysiques d'inducteurs et de transformateurs planaires Description de l'emploi Nous recherchons des personnes hautement motivées ayant une formation universitaire exceptionnelle qui souhaitent poursuivre un doctorat dans le domaine important et multidisciplinaire de recherche de la modélisation et de l'optimisation des dispositifs magnétiques planaires (inducteurs et transformateurs). Des dispositifs magnétiques planaires compacts et très efficaces utilisant par exemple des structures d'enroulement à base de PCB sont des composants clés de nombreux convertisseurs électroniques de puissance à profil bas, qui sont nécessaires par exemple pour les convertisseurs DC-DC (convertisseurs PoL) dans les futurs centres de données ou dans les applications automobiles pour l'interconnexion de la batterie d'entraînement principale avec la batterie auxiliaire 12V. Les dispositifs magnétiques planaires sont aussi souvent nécessaires dans les systèmes de recharge sans fil/transfert d'énergie, où ils doivent être très compacts et efficaces. Pour repousser les limites d'efficacité et de densité de puissance de ces appareils magnétiques planaires, vous développerez des modèles multiphysiques de magnétiques planaires. Ces modèles décrivent en détail les pertes (HF) dans les enroulements, les capacités parasitaires des enroulements, ainsi que la répartition de la température dans l'enroulement et aussi dans le noyau. De plus, vous développerez des modèles pour concevoir l'isolation électrique de l'enroulement. Sur la base de ces modèles, vous travaillerez à optimiser la géométrie du noyau et de l'enroulement, ainsi qu'à développer des concepts de refroidissement avancés pour les enroulements et le noyau. Sur la base des modèles et des concepts développés, vous identifierez ensuite les obstacles technologiques à la densité de puissance des magnétiques planaires. Les modèles développés devraient être intégrés dans les procédures d'optimisation des systèmes de convertisseur électronique de puissance d'une manière efficace par calcul. Cela est essentiel pour atteindre des gains d'efficacité et des densités de puissance remarquables et pour obtenir un avantage concurrentiel. Ces modèles font également partie d'un projet de développement d'un cadre de modélisation plus large et en cours à HPE, offrant la possibilité de collaborer avec d'autres doctorants sur divers aspects de la modélisation. Pour vérifier les nouveaux concepts de refroidissement et d'enroulement ainsi que les modèles développés, vous allez concevoir et construire différents prototypes, y compris les systèmes de convertisseur PE, pour faire fonctionner les magnétiques planaires dans des conditions réalistes. Notre laboratoire offre un poste stimulant et scientifiquement excitant à temps plein au sein d'une équipe internationale dynamique dans l'une des plus grandes universités techniques du monde. Nous encourageons également fortement la participation à des conférences internationales et offrons un salaire compétitif, d'excellents avantages et des installations de recherche et de laboratoire exceptionnelles pour vos expériences. Profil
• Vous devez avoir un diplôme / maîtrise en génie électrique avec d'excellentes qualités
• Connaissance fondamentale des systèmes de convertisseur électronique de puissance
• Bonnes compétences en communication
• Connaissance de l'anglais

Postdoctoral Researcher – Iterative Learning Control of Industrial Systems

100%, Zurich, permanent

print
Drucken

inspire AG is the leading Swiss competence centre for product innovation and advanced manufacturing. As a strategic partner of ETH Zurich, our mission is to transfer knowledge and technology from research to Swiss machine, electrical and metal industries.
The research group Control and Automation at inspire AG offers the following postdoctoral position as part of an industrial collaboration with a Swiss industry partner, and the Automatic Control Laboratory (IfA) at ETH Zurich.
Planned start date for the position is October 2026.

Project background

Our research group works on increasing the efficiency of industrial systems in real-world deployment by enabling process monitoring, learning, and policy training while ensuring safety and efficiency. For this, we develop novel learning-based control methods with practical applicability and theoretical guarantees.

Job description

We're looking for a skilled Postdoctoral Researcher to develop and deploy cutting-edge Iterative Learning Control (ILC) algorithms on real-world industrial platforms. The project requires good theoretical and hands-on expertise. Perfectly suited for those at the intersection of theory and application.

• Develop customized ILC and parameter optimization algorithms for industrial applications, going from theoretical analysis to implementation and testing on real systems

• Develop adaptive control and estimation schemes to support hardware implementation

• Collaborate closely with our industry partner to solve unique problems

Profile

• PhD degree in robotics, electrical or mechanical engineering, CS, or relevant fields

• Solid understanding of learning-based control methods and knowledge of iterative learning control theory with applications to industrial systems

• Excellent foundation in linear algebra, numerical methods, optimization, and control theory

• Background in online optimization theory and adaptive control theory is a plus

• Hands-on experience with industrial control systems is a plus

• An excellent knowledge (written/oral) of English is a must. Knowledge of German is beneficial

• Highly self-organized and structured way of working and solution orientation

• High motivation and willingness to learn new skills

• High level of teamwork, positive work attitude and creativity

• Willingness to supervise and support student projects

Workplace

We offer

We offer a full-time position for a postdoctoral researcher in our group as part our industrial collaboration project. Through the close cooperation with our project partner, you will quickly establish contacts to industry. In our young team you will work at the forefront of today's knowledge in learning-based industrial control.

Curious? So are we.

Please send your full application to our HR department hr@inspire.ch with the reference “ILC Postdoc” including the following documents:

• CV

• Cover letter

• Transcripts

• 2-3 reference contacts

• 2 representative publications
For technical questions, please contact Dr. Efe Balta, Head of Control and Automation ( efe.balta@inspire.ch ). Please also visit our website www.inspire.ch and the Automatic Control Lab https://control.ee.ethz.ch .

jobs.description:
PMO-Lead / Leitung Projektmanagement Office (m/w/d)

80%-100%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

Die ETH Zürich startet mit dem «Living Lab HIL» ein pionierhaftes Forschungsprojekt mit direktem Bezug zur Baupraxis. Das HIL-Gebäude auf dem Campus Hönggerberg wird zu einem Reallabor. Der sanierungsbedürftige Bau wird umgebaut und erweitert. In den kommenden Jahren erforschen und planen Professuren der Departemente Architektur (D-ARCH) sowie Bau, Umwelt und Geomatik (D-BAUG) die Sanierung des Gebäudes HIL im Sinne des zirkulären Bauens. Ziel ist es, das nachhaltige Entwerfen und Bauen im Bestand weiterzuentwickeln und exemplarisch an einem realen Planungs- und Bauprojekt zu anzuwenden.

Für den Aufbau, die Strukturierung und die operative Leitung unseres Living Lab HIL Projektmanagement-Offices (PMO) suchen wir eine organisationsstarke und durchsetzungsfähige Persönlichkeit als PMO-Lead, die eng mit der Geschäftsleitung arbeitet. Gemeinsam mit einer zu rekrutierenden Geschäftsleitungsassistenz sowie administrativer Unterstützung in den Bereichen Buchhaltung und Personalwesen bilden Sie das administrative und organisatorische Herzstück des Gesamtprojekts. Die Position bietet Raum für unterschiedliche Schwerpunkte in der Betriebsleitung und Ressourcensteuerung, sowie dem Stakeholder Management in einem anspruchsvollen Setting.

Stellenbeschreibung

In dieser projektbezogenen Rolle übernehmen Sie schwerpunktmässig folgende Aufgaben und Verantwortungen:

• Aufbau & Betriebsleitung: Verantwortung für die operative Betriebsleitung des Projektbüros Living Lab HIL sowie die Etablierung effizienter, transparenter PMO-Prozesse.

• „Planung der Planung“: Übergeordnete Termin-, Meilenstein- und Ressourcenplanung für das interdisziplinäre Gesamtprojekt in enger Abstimmung mit dem Planungsteam, internen ETH-Beteiligten und externen Projektpartnern.

• Stakeholder Management: Zentrale Drehscheibe für den Informationsfluss und die Kommunikation mit internen und externen Stakeholdern (Professuren, ETH Real Estate, externe Umsetzungspartner zB. Gesamtleister, Fachplaner).

• Ressourcenzuteilung & Controlling: Strategische Zuteilung von personellen und finanziellen Ressourcen sowie fortlaufendes Budgetcontrolling in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Geschäftsführer und der Buchhaltung.

• Vertrags- & Dokumentenmanagement: Strukturierung, Prüfung und verlässliche Verwaltung von Verträgen, Vereinbarungen und zentralen Projektdokumenten.

• Publikationen und Reporting: Koordination und Mitarbeit bei der Ausarbeitung Reportings und Präsentationen gemeinsam mit der internen Kommunikationsstelle.

• Sitzungsmanagement: Organisation, Vor- und Nachbereitung von Sitzungen, Workshops und Gremien inklusive Protokoll- und Pendenzenführung in Deutsch und Englisch.

• Teamführung: Führung des PMO-Teams in Abstimmung mit Geschäftsleitung.

• Die Stelle ist befristet bis maximal fünf Jahre, initial mit einem 1-Jahresvertrag mit Verlängerungsoptionen.

Profil

Um die Anforderungen dieser anspruchsvollen Position ideal zu erfüllen, bringen Sie folgendes Profil mit:

• Ausbildung: Abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (ETH/FH oder Universität) in Architektur, Bauingenieurwesen, Projektmanagement, Betriebswirtschaft oder einer vergleichbaren Disziplin.

• Berufserfahrung: Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Betriebsleitung, dem PMO-Management oder der übergeordneten Steuerung von komplexen Grossprojekten im Planungs- und Bauwesen oder im akademischen Umfeld.

• Methodenkompetenz: Ausgeprägte Fähigkeiten in der Strukturierung von Managementprozessen, Organisation, Ressourcenplanung und im Projektcontrolling.

• Administration & Recht: Sicheres Auftreten im Vertragswesen, tiefes Verständnis für administrative und operative Abläufe.

• Soft Skills: Strategisc

descriptionByLocale.it:
Ufficio di gestione del progetto (m/f/d) 80%-100%, Zurigo, temporaneo Stampato Stampa ETH Zurich lancia il Living Lab HIL, un progetto di ricerca pionieristico direttamente legato alla pratica dell'edilizia. L'edificio HIL del Campus Hönggerberg diventa un vero e proprio laboratorio. L'edificio in necessità di ristrutturazione sarà ricostruito e ampliato. Nei prossimi anni, i professori del Dipartimento di Architettura (D-ARCH) e Edilizia, Ambiente e Geomatica (D-BAUG) studieranno e pianificheranno la ristrutturazione dell'edificio HIL nel senso della costruzione circolare. L'obiettivo è quello di sviluppare ulteriormente il design e la costruzione sostenibili nell'area esistente e applicarlo come esempio ad un progetto di pianificazione e costruzione reale. Per la creazione, la strutturazione e la gestione operativa del nostro Living Lab HIL Project Management Office (PMO), stiamo cercando una personalità organizzativa forte e assertiva come un leader PMO che lavora a stretto contatto con la gestione. Insieme a un assistente di gestione da reclutare e supporto amministrativo nei settori della contabilità e delle risorse umane, si forma il cuore amministrativo e organizzativo del progetto generale. La posizione offre spazio per diverse aree di attenzione nella gestione delle operazioni e nella gestione delle risorse, nonché la gestione delle parti interessate in un contesto impegnativo. Descrizione del lavoro Assumere questo ruolo relativo al progetto Si concentrano sui seguenti compiti e responsabilità:
• Construction & Operations Management: Responsabilità per la gestione operativa dell'ufficio di progetto Living Lab HIL e la creazione di processi PMO efficienti e trasparenti.
• Pianificazione: pianificazione di piani, pietre miliari e risorse per il progetto interdisciplinare globale in stretto coordinamento con il team di pianificazione, i partecipanti ETH interni e i partner di progetto esterni.
• Stakeholder Management: hub centrale per il flusso di informazioni e comunicazione con gli stakeholder interni ed esterni (professori, ETH Real Estate, partner esterni di implementazione, ad esempio Gesamtleister, pianificatore specializzato).
• Allocation & Controlling delle risorse: allocazione strategica delle risorse umane e finanziarie e del bilancio in corso che controllano in collaborazione con l'amministratore delegato e la contabilità.
• Gestione dei contratti e dei documenti: esecuzione, verifica e gestione affidabile di contratti, accordi e documenti di progetto centrali.
• Pubblicazioni e relazioni: coordinamento e cooperazione nella preparazione di relazioni e presentazioni insieme all'ufficio comunicazioni interno.
• Gestione delle sessioni: organizzazione, preparazione e follow-up di incontri, workshop e comitati, tra cui protocollo e pendenze in tedesco e inglese.
• Leader del team: leadership del team PMO in coordinamento con la gestione.
• Il lavoro è limitato a un massimo di cinque anni, inizialmente con un contratto di 1 anno con opzioni di rinnovo. Profilo Per soddisfare idealmente i requisiti di questa posizione impegnativa, portare il seguente profilo:
• Istruzione: Studi universitari completi (ETH/FH o università) in architettura, ingegneria civile, gestione del progetto, amministrazione aziendale o una disciplina comparabile.
• Esperienza professionale: Diversi anni di esperienza nella gestione operativa, nella gestione PMO o nella gestione a più alto livello di complessi progetti su larga scala nella pianificazione e nella costruzione o nell'ambiente accademico.
• Competenza metodologica: Forti competenze nella strutturazione dei processi di gestione, organizzazione, pianificazione delle risorse e controllo del progetto.
• Amministrazione e Diritto: Presenza sicura nel contratto, profonda comprensione dei processi amministrativi e operativi.
• Abilità morbide: Strategisc
descriptionByLocale.en:
PMO-Lead / Head of Project Management Office (m/f/d) 80%-100%, Zurich, temporary Printed Printing ETH Zurich is launching the Living Lab HIL, a pioneering research project directly related to building practice. The HIL building on Campus Hönggerberg becomes a real laboratory. The building in need of renovation will be rebuilt and expanded. In the coming years, professorships in the Department of Architecture (D-ARCH) and Construction, Environment and Geomatics (D-BAUG) will research and plan the renovation of the HIL building in the sense of circular construction. The aim is to further develop sustainable design and construction in the existing area and to apply it as an example to a real planning and construction project. For the establishment, structuring and operational management of our Living Lab HIL Project Management Office (PMO), we are looking for an organizationally strong and assertive personality as a PMO lead who works closely with the management. Together with a management assistant to be recruited as well as administrative support in the areas of accounting and human resources, you form the administrative and organizational heart of the overall project. The position offers space for different focus areas in operations management and resource management, as well as stakeholder management in a demanding setting. Job description Taking on this project-related role They focus on the following tasks and responsibilities:
• Construction & Operations Management: Responsibility for the operational management of the Living Lab HIL project office and the establishment of efficient, transparent PMO processes.
• Planning: Overarching schedule, milestone and resource planning for the interdisciplinary overall project in close coordination with the planning team, internal ETH participants and external project partners.
• Stakeholder Management: Central hub for the flow of information and communication with internal and external stakeholders (professorships, ETH Real Estate, external implementation partners e.g. Gesamtleister, specialist planner).
• Resource Allocation & Controlling: Strategic allocation of human and financial resources as well as ongoing budget controlling in cooperation with the managing director and accounting.
• Contract & Document Management: Structuring, auditing and reliable management of contracts, agreements and central project documents.
• Publications and reporting: coordination and cooperation in the preparation of reports and presentations together with the internal communications office.
• Session management: organisation, preparation and follow-up of meetings, workshops and committees, including protocol and pendences in German and English.
• Team leadership: leadership of the PMO team in coordination with management.
• The job is limited to a maximum of five years, initially with a 1-year contract with renewal options. Profile To ideally meet the requirements of this demanding position, bring the following profile:
• Education: Completed university studies (ETH/FH or university) in architecture, civil engineering, project management, business administration or a comparable discipline.
• Professional experience: Several years of experience in operational management, PMO management or the higher-level management of complex large-scale projects in planning and construction or in the academic environment.
• Methodological competence: Strong skills in structuring management processes, organization, resource planning and project controlling.
• Administration & Law: Secure presence in contracting, deep understanding of administrative and operational processes.
• Soft Skills: Strategisc
